title: Add direct unit tests for MouseCursorManager (services)
body:
`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/mouse_cursor.dart` defines `MouseCursorManager`, the class that implements the cursor candidate resolution protocol used by `MouseTracker`. It has no dedicated test file: searching the test tree, the class is only exercised indirectly via `MouseTracker`-based tests (e.g. `rendering/mouse_tracker_test.dart`, `widgets/mouse_region_test.dart`).

The manager's specified behavior would benefit from direct unit tests that lock it down without a running tracker or a widget tree:

* `MouseCursor.defer` is rejected as the fallback cursor.
* The first non-deferred candidate is selected; empty or all-deferred candidate lists fall back.
* Re-resolving an already-active cursor is a no-op, with or without a triggering `PointerEvent`.
* When the cursor changes, the old session is disposed before the new session is activated.
* Devices are tracked independently; a cursor can hold sessions on multiple devices at once.
* `PointerRemovedEvent` clears the bookkeeping for a device without disposing its session.
* `debugDeviceActiveCursor` returns the last activated cursor and null for unknown devices.

I have a patch ready that adds `packages/flutter/test/services/mouse_cursor_test.dart` covering the above.

title: [tool] build ios-framework keeps a Generated.xcconfig written by a different Flutter SDK
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create -t module m && cd m` (any Flutter SDK).
2. Delete `.ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig`, then run `flutter pub get` with SDK A. The file now has `FLUTTER_ROOT=<SDK A>`.
3. Run `flutter build ios-framework` with a different SDK, SDK B.

### Expected results

The build uses SDK B. Afterwards `.ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig` names SDK B, as it does after `flutter build ios`.

### Actual results

The file still names SDK A. The build's `pod install` step reads `FLUTTER_ROOT` from it, so it runs against SDK A. If SDK A has no iOS engine artifacts, the build fails:

```
<SDK A>/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/ios/Flutter.xcframework must exist
```

If SDK A does have them, the plugin frameworks build against SDK A's engine.

The cause: `build ios-framework` regenerates `Generated.xcconfig` only through `_updateGeneratedXcodeConfigIfNeeded`, which skips the file when it is newer than the running SDK's `bin/cache/flutter_tools.stamp`. `flutter build ios` and `build ipa` call `updateGeneratedXcodeProperties` on every build (in `buildXcodeProject`), so they don't have this problem.

In practice, SDK A is usually an IDE running `pub get` with a different SDK than the one used on the command line.

### Flutter Doctor output

Not doctor-dependent. Reproduced on macOS with a build of the tool based on the current stable release. The code is the same on master at 66b3ad9017, and a hermetic test against master shows the same behavior (it's in the linked PR).

flutter build ios-framework fails to find the code-signing identity on a module without .ios/
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create -t module mod && cd mod`
2. `rm -rf .ios` (it's generated and usually gitignored, so this is what a fresh CI checkout looks like)
3. `FLUTTER_XCODE_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<your team> flutter build ios-framework --no-debug --no-profile`

(With exactly one Apple Development identity for that team in the keychain.)

### Expected results

The frameworks build and are signed with the team's identity, which is what happens if you run step 3 a second time.

### Actual results

```
Finding code-signing identities...
No valid code-signing identity found. Please specify which identity to use with --codesign-identity or use --no-codesign.
```

Since #183399, `BuildIOSFrameworkCommand.runCommand` looks up the code-signing identity (which reads `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` from `.ios/Runner.xcodeproj` via `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings`) before the build loop calls `regeneratePlatformSpecificToolingIfApplicable`, which is what creates `.ios/` for a module. On a fresh checkout the project doesn't exist yet when it is read, so no team is found. The first run fails, and later runs succeed because the failed run left `.ios/` behind.

### Flutter Doctor output

Reproduced on macOS with Xcode installed, using a 3.47 build of the tool (Shorebird's fork, whose `build_ios_framework.dart` has this same order). `master`'s `runCommand` has the same order.

body:
### Use case

I would like to be able to create a Docker container with the following setup:

- Install Flutter as root, so it is read-only by everyone else (locked down, not possible to update).
- Run Dart and Flutter tools as a `flutter` user inside the container (without getting weird warnings and errors).
- Test and build using the non-privileged `flutter`-user accessing the application source code read-only (e.g. via a bind mount).
- Write build artifacts elsewhere outside the source code. If Flutter only needs to write in a single directory, this could be solved by bind mounting a directory from the host.

It isn't enough to just mount a Gradle and pub cache. Flutter also wants to write to `flutter/bin/cache` on every evocation and but that cache seems to hard coupled to files in `flutter/packages/flutter_tools/` as well making it a very complex setup. After many hacks and tumbling down the Flutter/Docker rabbit hole, I cam to the realization that Flutter just makes this hard/impossible - at least if you don't have intimately Flutter-knowledge.
It might possible to make "all things Flutter" world-writeable (`777`), but that isn't really an acceptable solution in my opinion.

Thanks for an interesting project.

### Proposal

I suspect a lot of things makes this request very hard if not impossible.
But one can dream 😅

title: TableBorder.lerp and TableBorder.scale drop borderRadius
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```dart
final a = TableBorder.all(borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(4)));
final b = TableBorder.all(borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(12)));

print(TableBorder.lerp(a, b, 0.5)!.borderRadius); // BorderRadius.zero
print(b.scale(0.5).borderRadius);                 // BorderRadius.zero
```

### Expected results

`lerp` interpolates the radius (8 here), and `scale` scales it (6 here), the same way `BoxDecoration` handles `borderRadius`.

### Actual results

Both return `BorderRadius.zero`. `TableBorder.lerp` and `TableBorder.scale` build a new `TableBorder` from the six sides only, so a table with rounded corners loses them for the whole of an animation, for example when the table's border animates through a theme change. `TableBorder.lerp(null, b, t)` goes through `scale`, so animating a rounded border in from nothing is affected too.

### Flutter version

`master` and stable 3.47.8.

title: [camera_platform_interface] VideoRecordedEvent == and hashCode disagree
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```dart
final a = VideoRecordedEvent(1, XFile('/tmp/video.mp4'), null);
final b = VideoRecordedEvent(1, XFile('/tmp/video.mp4'), null);
print(a == b);                 // true
print(a.hashCode == b.hashCode); // false

final c = VideoRecordedEvent(1, XFile('/tmp/other.mp4'), null);
print(a == c);                 // true
```

### Expected results

Events that are `==` have the same `hashCode`, and events for different video files aren't equal.

### Actual results

`VideoRecordedEvent.operator ==` doesn't compare `file`, but `hashCode` hashes the `XFile` object itself. `XFile` has no value equality, so:

- two events for the same recording (for example, one created by `VideoRecordedEvent.fromJson`) are `==` but have different hash codes, which breaks the `==`/`hashCode` contract and makes them misbehave in sets and maps;
- two events for different files compare equal.

### Package version

camera_platform_interface 2.15.0 (`main` as of today)

title: [gestures] latestPointer switches control to a stationary second finger when the first finger starts a drag
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample on a device that supports two simultaneous touch contacts.
2. Put finger 1 down inside the blue area and keep it pressed.
3. Put finger 2 down inside the same area before moving either finger. Keep finger 2 stationary.
4. Move finger 1 horizontally until the drag threshold is exceeded and `drag START` is emitted.
5. Continue moving finger 1 while keeping finger 2 stationary.
6. Move finger 2, then lift finger 2 and move finger 1 again.

The sample explicitly configures `MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer`. A competing tap recognizer keeps the gesture arena contested so that the drag is accepted after movement exceeds the threshold, rather than immediately after pointer down.

### Expected results

The finger whose movement starts the drag should continue to produce drag updates while it remains down, without requiring the user to move a different, stationary finger.

This is a proposed interaction expectation, rather than a claim that the implementation contradicts the existing API documentation. Please clarify whether this pre-acceptance multi-pointer handoff is intentional. If it is intentional, documenting this specific case would help explain the otherwise surprising loss of updates.

### Actual results

Finger 1 starts the drag, but its subsequent movement does not produce `onUpdate` callbacks while finger 2 remains down. Moving finger 2 produces updates. After finger 2 is lifted, finger 1 can drive updates again.

As a result, the drag appears to stop responding immediately after it starts, even though the finger that initiated the drag is still moving.

The [API documentation](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/gestures/DragGestureRecognizer/multitouchDragStrategy.html) defines `latestPointer` in terms of the latest active pointer accepted by the recognizer. The current implementation explains the handoff:

- Crossing the threshold calls `resolve(GestureDisposition.accepted)` for the recognizer's pending pointers.
- `acceptGesture(pointer)` assigns `_activePointer = pointer` on each acceptance.
- When pointer 1 and then pointer 2 are accepted, pointer 2 becomes active even though it has not moved.
- Subsequent move events from pointer 1 are excluded from drag updates by `_shouldTrackMoveEvent`.

Relevant source at the local checkout revision:

- [Threshold acceptance and active pointer selection](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6be76865c49874d5745bb3618ec7fd7797622f2f/packages/flutter/lib/src/gestures/monodrag.dart#L704-L745)
- [Move event filtering](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6be76865c49874d5745bb3618ec7fd7797622f2f/packages/flutter/lib/src/gestures/monodrag.dart#L450-L461)

```dart
import 'package:flutter/gestures.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: DragDemo()));

class DragDemo extends StatefulWidget {
  const DragDemo({super.key});

  @override
  State<DragDemo> createState() => _DragDemoState();
}

class _DragDemoState extends State<DragDemo> {
  final List<String> _logs = <String>[];
  int _sequence = 0;
  double _distance = 0;

  void _log(String message) {
    final line = '${++_sequence}: $message';
    debugPrint(line);
    setState(() {
      _logs.insert(0, line);
      if (_logs.length > 60) {
        _logs.removeLast();
      }
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('latestPointer reproduction')),
      body: SafeArea(
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
          children: <Widget>[
            const Padding(
              padding: EdgeInsets.all(16),
              child: Text(
                'Use two fingers on a touch screen.\n'
                '1. Hold finger 1, then hold finger 2.\n'
                '2. Keep finger 2 still; drag finger 1 horizontally.\n'
                '3. After START, keep moving finger 1: no UPDATE.\n'
                '4. Move finger 2: UPDATE resumes.\n'
                '5. Lift finger 2; finger 1 can drive UPDATE again.',
              ),
            ),
            RawGestureDetector(
              behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
              gestures: <Type, GestureRecognizerFactory>{
                LoggingDragRecognizer:
                    GestureRecognizerFactoryWithHandlers<LoggingDragRecognizer>(
                      () => LoggingDragRecognizer(_log),
                      (LoggingDragRecognizer instance) {
                        instance
                          ..multitouchDragStrategy = MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer
                          ..onDown = (DragDownDetails details) {
                            _log('drag DOWN');
                          }
                          ..onStart = (DragStartDetails details) {
                            _log('drag START');
                          }
                          ..onUpdate = (DragUpdateDetails details) {
                            _distance += details.delta.dx;
                            _log(
                              'drag UPDATE from p${instance.eventPointer}: '
                              'dx=${details.delta.dx.toStringAsFixed(1)}',
                            );
                          }
                          ..onEnd = (DragEndDetails details) {
                            _log('drag END');
                          }
                          ..onCancel = () {
                            _log('drag CANCEL');
                          };
                      },
                    ),
                // Keep the arena contested until movement exceeds drag slop.
                // A lone drag recognizer can win immediately after pointer down.
                TapGestureRecognizer: GestureRecognizerFactoryWithHandlers<TapGestureRecognizer>(
                  TapGestureRecognizer.new,
                  (TapGestureRecognizer instance) {
                    instance.onTap = () => _log('TAP');
                  },
                ),
              },
              child: Listener(
                behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
                onPointerDown: (PointerDownEvent event) => _log('raw DOWN p${event.pointer}'),
                onPointerMove: (PointerMoveEvent event) => _log(
                  'raw MOVE p${event.pointer}: dx=${event.delta.dx.toStringAsFixed(1)}',
                ),
                onPointerUp: (PointerUpEvent event) => _log('raw UP p${event.pointer}'),
                onPointerCancel: (PointerCancelEvent event) => _log('raw CANCEL p${event.pointer}'),
                child: Container(
                  height: 180,
                  color: Colors.lightBlue.shade100,
                  alignment: Alignment.center,
                  child: Text('Drag here\nTotal dx: ${_distance.toStringAsFixed(1)}'),
                ),
              ),
            ),
            const Padding(
              padding: EdgeInsets.all(8),
              child: Text('Logs (newest first; also printed to console)'),
            ),
            Expanded(
              child: ListView.builder(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12),
                itemCount: _logs.length,
                itemBuilder: (BuildContext context, int index) => Text(_logs[index]),
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

class LoggingDragRecognizer extends HorizontalDragGestureRecognizer {
  LoggingDragRecognizer(this.log);

  final ValueChanged<String> log;
  int? eventPointer;

  @override
  void handleEvent(PointerEvent event) {
    eventPointer = event.pointer;
    super.handleEvent(event);
    eventPointer = null;
  }

  @override
  void acceptGesture(int pointer) {
    log('acceptGesture(p$pointer) ENTER');
    super.acceptGesture(pointer);
    log('acceptGesture(p$pointer) EXIT');
  }
}

title: [cupertino_ui] OverlayVisibilityMode.editing and .notEditing ignore focus
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

cupertino_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  cupertino_ui:
    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: cupertino_ui
      sha256: a47c4e7c66fd7444a063a602597fceb238f705c3f6b1322bc0053d0a2638ee6e
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.1.4"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample on iOS.
2. Type into the first field, then tap the second.

### Expected results

The first field's clear button goes away once you leave it, like UIKit's [`.whileEditing`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uitextfield/viewmode/whileediting).

### Actual results

It stays. `_shouldShowAttachment` in `text_field.dart` only checks for text (`editing => hasText`, `notEditing => !hasText`) and never looks at focus. Main has the same code, and the enum's docs describe it that way too, but the UIKit modes these mirror follow focus.

So `notEditing` disagrees with UIKit's [`.unlessEditing`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uitextfield/viewmode/unlessediting) in 3 of 4 cases, and `always` puts an X on an empty field, which UIKit never does.

| Does the X show? | `editing` | UIKit `.whileEditing` | `notEditing` | UIKit `.unlessEditing` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, not focused | no | no | yes | no |
| Empty, focused | no | no | yes | no |
| Text, not focused | yes | no | no | yes |
| Text, focused | yes | yes | no | no |

<details><summary>prefixMode and suffixMode</summary>

Same rule here. UIKit's `leftViewMode` and `rightViewMode` follow focus too, with one twist: `.unlessEditing` keeps the view on a focused field until there's text in it.

| Does the view show? | `editing` | UIKit `.whileEditing` | `notEditing` | UIKit `.unlessEditing` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, not focused | no | no | yes | yes |
| Empty, focused | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Text, not focused | yes | no | no | yes |
| Text, focused | yes | yes | no | no |

</details>

I checked UIKit on the iOS 26.2 simulator and cupertino_ui in a widget test.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:cupertino_ui/cupertino_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(
  const CupertinoApp(
    home: CupertinoPageScaffold(
      child: SafeArea(
        child: Column(
          children: [
            CupertinoTextField(clearButtonMode: OverlayVisibilityMode.editing),
            CupertinoTextField(placeholder: 'Tap here to leave the first field'),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    ),
  ),
);
```

</details>

<details><summary>UIKit</summary>

```swift
let field = UITextField()
field.clearButtonMode = .whileEditing
```

</details>

title: [Android] TextField context menu does not show on long press after focus returns with an unchanged selection
EditableText does not update RenderEditable.hasFocus or its semantics isFocused when it regains focus with a valid selection
SpellCheckConfiguration == and hashCode ignore misspelledSelectionColor
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```dart
const red = SpellCheckConfiguration(misspelledSelectionColor: Color(0xFFFF0000));
const blue = SpellCheckConfiguration(misspelledSelectionColor: Color(0xFF0000FF));
print(red == blue); // true
```

Then rebuild an `EditableText` whose `spellCheckConfiguration` differs only in `misspelledSelectionColor` (same service and text style).

### Expected results

`red == blue` is `false`, and `EditableText` uses the new `misspelledSelectionColor`.

### Actual results

`SpellCheckConfiguration.operator ==` and `hashCode` don't include `misspelledSelectionColor` (added in #125162), so the two configurations compare equal. `EditableTextState.didUpdateWidget` only re-infers `_spellCheckConfiguration` when `oldWidget.spellCheckConfiguration != widget.spellCheckConfiguration`, so it keeps using the old selection color for misspelled words.

### Flutter version

`master` and stable 3.47.8.

body:
### Help us understand the severity of this issue

- [ ] causing severe production issues e.g. malfunctions or data loss
- [ ] blocking next binary release
- [x] blocking a client feature launch within a quarter
- [ ] nice-to-have but does not block a launch within the next quarter

### Steps to reproduce

Enable Talkback
1. Using swipe forward gesture, swipe through the list.
2. When you reach the end of the list, swipe backwards through the list

### Expected results

The previous list item should be focused when moving focus backwards.

### Actual results

Rather than focusing the direct-previous list item, the list instead scrolls all the way up, with the focus ring dropping down with the item that was focused previously until the list scrolls all the way up and the focus ring moves to the top item.

title: Android platform views receive inconsistent pointer ids when a pointer lifts and another lands in the same frame
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Flutter app with a full-screen `AndroidView` (an `EagerGestureRecognizer` is set, so every pointer is forwarded).
2. In the native view, log every `MotionEvent` with its pointer ids, and flag events that are impossible given the earlier ones (e.g. `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down).
3. On a physical device, keep one finger down and repeatedly lift one finger while landing another at nearly the same moment (a "drumming" motion with 2–3 extra fingers).

In our test, 3 out of 8 such gestures produced an invalid stream within ~30 seconds.

### Expected results

The platform view receives a consistent pointer stream, as it would when hosted natively: each pointer id goes down once, keeps its id until it goes up, and every `MOVE` contains exactly the pointers that are down.

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(2)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]
```

### Actual results

The same finger is reported under different ids. The platform view receives `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down, `ACTION_POINTER_UP` for an id that never went down, and `MOVE` events whose pointer set changes without any down/up event:

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(2) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638   <- id 2 is already down
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688   <- lifts id 1, but the finger that lifted is id 2
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]                  <- id 2 disappears, id 1 stays
```

Native gesture code that tracks pointers by id breaks on this stream. For example, [mapbox-gestures-android](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gestures-android) throws `IllegalArgumentException: invalid pointerIndex -1` and `NullPointerException` ([mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter#1146](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter/issues/1146)), and those exceptions reach Dart as unhandled `PlatformException`s from `AndroidViewController.sendMotionEvent`.

#### Cause

Two id assignments are mixed in the stream the platform view receives:

1. **Dart assigns its own Android pointer ids.** `_AndroidMotionEventConverter.handlePointerDownEvent` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/platform_views.dart`) gives each new pointer the lowest id that is not in `usedAndroidPointerIds`, and frees an id as soon as it handles the pointer up. Android keeps the id of a lifted pointer reserved until the end of the input frame in which it lifted. So when a finger lifts and another lands in the **same frame**, Android gives the new finger a fresh id (2), but Dart reuses the id it just freed (1). From then on, Dart's ids and Android's ids for the same finger differ.

2. **The engine sends a mix of original and rebuilt events.** `PlatformViewsController.toMotionEvent` returns the original Android `MotionEvent` (with Android's ids) when its pointer count and action match the framework's event. Otherwise it rebuilds the event from the framework's pointer properties (with Dart's ids). This was added in #178528 (the fix for #176574). The check compares only the pointer count and action, not the pointer ids.

When the ids have diverged, `MOVE` events usually match and pass through with Android's ids. `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` events often don't, because Dart orders pointers by insertion and Android orders them by id, so the action index differs. Those events are rebuilt with Dart's ids. The platform view gets both kinds of event, so a finger's id appears to change.

Framework-side trace of the same moment (debug prints added locally to `_AndroidMotionEventConverter`; `androidId` is decoded from `event.device`):

```console
free   pointer=18 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                                t=15800488
assign pointer=19 androidId=2 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                    t=15800488  <- same frame: Android picks 2, Dart reuses 1
...
assign pointer=20 androidId=1 dartId=2 used={0, 1, 2}                t=15800638  <- Android reuses 1, Dart picks 2
send   _TransformedPointerDownEvent action=517 dartIds=[0, 1, 2]                  <- action index differs, so the engine rebuilds it with Dart's ids
```

Possible fixes: have `_AndroidMotionEventConverter` use Android's pointer id (it is already available in `PointerEvent.device`) instead of assigning its own, or have `toMotionEvent` compare pointer ids as well before reusing the original event.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/gestures.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: ReproPage()));

class ReproPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const ReproPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: AndroidView(
        viewType: 'touch-checker',
        layoutDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
        creationParamsCodec: const StandardMessageCodec(),
        gestureRecognizers: <Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>>{
          Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>(() => EagerGestureRecognizer()),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

```kotlin
class TouchCheckerView(context: Context) : View(context) {
  private val downIds = mutableSetOf<Int>()

  override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    val ids = (0 until event.pointerCount).map { event.getPointerId(it) }
    val actionId = event.getPointerId(event.actionIndex)
    Log.d(TAG, "${MotionEvent.actionToString(event.action)} ids=$ids t=${event.eventTime}")

    val expected = when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds + actionId
      else -> downIds.toSet()
    }
    when {
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN && actionId in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_DOWN for id $actionId, which is already down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP && actionId !in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_UP for id $actionId, which is not down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked != MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL && ids.toSet() != expected ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: event has ids $ids, expected $expected")
    }

    when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> { downIds.clear(); downIds += actionId }
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds += actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP -> downIds -= actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> downIds.clear()
    }
    return true
  }
}

title: [Impeller] EGL_BAD_ACCESS after returning to the foreground, then no frames at all (Mali-G57, OpenGLES)
body:
### Steps to reproduce ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the app, look something up (a WebView with dictionary content is on screen), then leave it — the task stays in recents, the activity is stopped but not destroyed. 2. From another app, share text to this app. The share entry is an invisible `ProcessTextActivity` that starts the existing `singleTop` `MainActivity` with `NEW_TASK | CLEAR_TOP | SINGLE_TOP`, then finishes. 3. The window comes back black, and stays black. It happens on roughly every second such entry on this device, and never after a plain home → recents → tap cycle. See the attached `black.mp4` (the black segment starts around 16.5 s) and `ok.mp4` for the same steps on the same device with `EnableImpeller=false`, where it works. App: https://github.com/mumu-lhl/Ciyue (open source, Flutter 3.47.5, release build) ### Expected results ## Expected results The UI redraws as before, as it does in `ok.mp4`. ### Actual results ## Actual results The window stays black for the rest of the process lifetime. The app is alive: the UI thread runs, Dart receives the intent (the lookup the share asked for does happen), back navigation responds. ``` ActivityTaskManager: START u0 {act=android.intent.action.PROCESS_TEXT ... flg=0x34000000 cmp=.../MainActivity} BufferQueueDebug: [SurfaceView[...MainActivity](BLAST)#400066] <- new surface E flutter: [ERROR:flutter/impeller/toolkit/egl/egl.cc(56)] EGL Error: Bad Access (12290) in .../impeller/toolkit/egl/context.cc:55 E flutter: [ERROR:flutter/shell/gpu/gpu_surface_gl_impeller.cc(76)] Could not make the context current to acquire the frame. ActivityTaskManager: Displayed .../MainActivity: +85ms <- "displayed" (no BufferQueueProducer queueBuffer for that SurfaceView afterwards) ``` The system considers the window displayed (`Displayed ... +85ms`) while the engine never submits another buffer. On every resume that recovers, the engine logs a new context (`android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104): Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).`); in the failing resume that line is absent. ## Isolation Same app, same commit, same device; only the named line changes. Each row is reproducible by toggling one line and rebuilding. | Build | What differs | Result | |---|---|---| | as shipped | `useHybridComposition: true` in the InAppWebView settings | **black + EGL_BAD_ACCESS** | | A | that line set to `false` (surface composition) | renders | | B | WebView replaced by a `Text` (no platform view at all) | renders | | C | whole Dart UI replaced by ten lines (Android shell and all plugins kept) | renders | | D | `EnableImpeller=false` (Skia) | renders | So Impeller, texture-layer hybrid composition and a real WebView are all required: remove any one of the four and the app is fine. ## Minimal reproduction attempt (negative result) Two attempts, both with a `singleTop` activity and an invisible `ProcessTextActivity` forwarding `ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT`: 1. `PlatformViewsService.initExpensiveAndroidView` with a plain native `TextView` — no reproduction (16 cycles, no EGL errors). 2. The real `flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 with `useHybridComposition: true`, `transparentBackground: true` and `baseUrl: http://ciyue.internal/`, the app's own settings — no reproduction either. Project: https://github.com/yx-wh/impeller-platform-view-repro Remaining differences: the app's word view is a `PageView`, so several platform views exist at the same time; the WebView loads through `webViewAssetLoader` plus custom schemes (`entry`, `gdlookup`, `sound`); and the app does a large startup (dictionaries, isolates) before the first frame. I am happy to bisect along whichever you think is most likely. ### Code sample
Code sample The sample does **not** reproduce the failure — it is the closest reduction I could reach. Full project: https://github.com/yx-wh/impeller-platform-view-repro The essential parts: ```dart // lib/main.dart class _ExpensivePlatformView extends StatelessWidget { const _ExpensivePlatformView(); @override Widget build(BuildContext context) { return PlatformViewLink( viewType: "repro/view", surfaceFactory: (context, controller) => PlatformViewSurface( controller: controller, gestureRecognizers: const >{}, hitTestBehavior: PlatformViewHitTestBehavior.opaque, ), onCreatePlatformView: (params) { return PlatformViewsService.initExpensiveAndroidView( id: params.id, viewType: params.viewType, layoutDirection: Directionality.of(context), creationParamsCodec: const StandardMessageCodec(), onFocus: () => params.onFocusChanged(true), ) ..addOnPlatformViewCreatedListener(params.onPlatformViewCreated) ..create(); }, ); } } ``` ```kotlin // MainActivity.kt — singleTop, receives the forwarded intent override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent) { super.onNewIntent(intent) setIntent(intent) val text = intent.getCharSequenceExtra(Intent.EXTRA_PROCESS_TEXT)?.toString() if (text != null) channel?.invokeMethod("text", text) } // ProcessTextActivity.kt — invisible entry point val intent = Intent(this, MainActivity::class.java).apply { action = Intent.ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_PROCESS_TEXT, text) addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK) addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP) } startActivity(intent) finish() ```
### Screenshots or Video
Screenshots / Video demonstration - `black.mp4` — Impeller build: the window is black from ~16.5 s to ~21.2 s (only the status and navigation bars are drawn), then back navigation returns to the reader, so the process is alive. - `ok.mp4` — same device, same steps, `EnableImpeller=false`: the UI renders. - `black-frame.png` / `skia-frame.png` — single frames from each clip.

title: [web] iOS Safari: Japanese IME duplicates composed text in a TextField with enableInteractiveSelection: false
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the code sample below for the web and open it in Safari on iOS.
2. Add the Japanese Kana keyboard (Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard > Japanese > Kana) and switch to it with the globe key.
3. Tap the "selection off" field. On the 12-key Kana layout, tap は, tap な, then choose the candidate 花.
4. Do the same in the "default" field and in the "selection off, single-line" field.

Reproduced on the iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 27.0, Safari 27.0, with a debug web build on Flutter 3.47.7 stable. The same duplication also showed up in a Flutter web app that uses `enableInteractiveSelection: false`, on the iOS 18.6 Simulator (Safari 18.6) and on a real iPhone (iOS 18.7.1, Safari). Desktop Safari was not tested.

### Expected results

Every field composes in place, as the default field does: は, then はな, then 花.

### Actual results

The two "selection off" fields set `enableInteractiveSelection: false`.

| Field                              | after は | after な | after 花 |
|------------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| selection off (textarea)           | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |
| default (textarea)                 | は       | はな     | 花       |
| selection off, single-line (input) | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |

Each key after the first re-inserts the whole preedit at the caret, and choosing the candidate appends it instead of replacing the preedit. The field keeps the duplicated text: the hidden DOM element and the rendered field both end with ははな花.

---

**Cause**

On iOS Safari, `IOSTextEditingStrategy` routes the hidden element's `input` event and the document's `selectionchange` to `DefaultTextEditingStrategy.handleChange`, which first calls `suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`. When `enableInteractiveSelection` is false and the DOM selection is not collapsed, that function collapses the selection to its end and writes it back with `EditingState.applyToDomElement` (`value = text`, then `setSelectionRange`). The write happens synchronously inside the event, and nothing checks for an active composition.

WebKit dispatches each `insertCompositionText` input event while the selection spans the marked text (`[0,1]`, `[1,3]` and `[3,4]` in the log below). The engine collapses that selection during the event. After that, WebKit no longer treats the text as marked, but it never fires `compositionend`. The next key therefore starts a new composition at the caret with the whole preedit as its data, and the candidate arrives as one more composition inserted at the caret.

- 3.47.7: [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1617-L1642), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1644-L1660), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1065-L1079)
- main (aebd23e2d4): [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1800-L1825), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1827-L1843), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1191-L1205). The function is unchanged on main.

`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded` was added in #171935, which first shipped in 3.35.0. I have not bisected this.

**Suggested fix**

Skip the DOM write while a composition is active, but still return the collapsed state to the framework. This is the same approach as the existing guard in `updateElementPlacement`, which skips `placeElement()` while `composingText != null` (#98817, fixed by flutter/engine#51323; [3.47.7](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1541-L1555), [main](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1713-L1727)):

```dart
    final EditingState newEditingState = editingState.copyWith(
      baseOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
      extentOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
    );
    // Writing the DOM selection mid-composition makes WebKit drop the
    // composition without a compositionend. See also #98817.
    if (composingText == null) {
      newEditingState.applyToDomElement(activeDomElement);
    }
    return newEditingState;
```

`compositionupdate` sets `composingText` before the `input` event, so the check covers both the `input` and the `selectionchange` paths. `InputEvent.isComposing` would cover only `input`. I have not tested this patch.

This is related to #193847 (fixed by #194096) but is a different bug: that one is a stale composing range after the framework rewrites the text in the middle of a composition.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart

// Repro: iOS Safari + Japanese Kana keyboard duplicates composed text in a
// TextField with enableInteractiveSelection: false. Compose は, な, then 花.
void main() => runApp(const ReproApp());

class ReproApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const ReproApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: SafeArea(
          child: Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.all(16),
            child: Column(
              children: [
                TextField(
                  enableInteractiveSelection: false,
                  maxLines: null,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'selection off'),
                ),
                SizedBox(height: 16),
                TextField(
                  maxLines: null,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'default'),
                ),
                SizedBox(height: 16),
                TextField(
                  enableInteractiveSelection: false,
                  maxLines: 1,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'selection off, single-line'),
                ),
              ],
            ),

    );

}

[camera_android_camerax] takePicture sets an unchanged flash mode on every capture
body:
**Once an app calls `setFlashMode`, every `takePicture()` sets the same flash mode on
`ImageCapture` again, which adds roughly 250-300 ms to each capture.** This happens
even when the mode is `FlashMode.off` and never changes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.high`.
2. Call `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)`.
3. Call `takePicture()` repeatedly and measure the latency.

### Results

| | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `setFlashMode` never called | 517 ms | 360 ms |
| `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)` called once | **794 ms** | **656 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart. "ZSL on" means
`setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.

### Why

`takePicture` calls `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` before every capture whenever a
flash mode has been set (since flutter/packages#3800). CameraX keeps the flash mode
on the `ImageCapture` instance for subsequent captures, so the repeated call does not
change anything. In CameraX 1.6.2, `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` has no check for an
unchanged mode, so each call still goes through `CameraControl.setFlashMode`. (The
androidx-main source has since added that check.)

### Proposed fix

Only call `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` in `takePicture` when the mode differs from the
one last applied to the current `ImageCapture` instance. The torch behavior from
flutter/packages#4903 (clearing a previous flash mode when torch is enabled) stays
the same.

title: [camera_android_camerax] Zero-shutter-lag has no effect with ResolutionPreset.max
body:
**With `ResolutionPreset.max`, zero-shutter-lag (ZSL) has no effect, so none of the
`ResolutionPreset`s gives full-resolution photos with ZSL.** The other presets work
with ZSL, but cap the photo size (`high`: 1280x720; `ultraHigh` requests 16:9 up to
3840x2160).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.max` on a device where
   `isZeroShutterLagSupported()` returns `true`.
2. Call `setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.
3. Measure `takePicture()` latency.

### Results

Every call succeeds and nothing is logged, but capture latency does not change:

| Preset | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `ResolutionPreset.high` | 517 ms | **360 ms** |
| `ResolutionPreset.max` | 828 ms | **826 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart.

### Why

**CameraX turns ZSL off when any bound use case prefers higher resolution over
capture rate, and `ResolutionPreset.max` sets that on every use case** (since
flutter/packages#11956).

This is not in the `ImageCapture` docs, which list only `VideoCapture`, flash and
extensions. In CameraX 1.6.2, `UseCase.mergeConfigs()` sets `OPTION_ZSL_DISABLED` on
any use case whose `ResolutionSelector` uses a non-default allowed resolution mode,
and ZSL is turned off if any bound use case has that flag.

### Proposed fix

- When ZSL is enabled, `ResolutionPreset.max` uses the largest regular size for still
  capture, that is, the largest size in the normal output size list rather than the
  separate high-resolution list (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`). Without ZSL, still
  capture with `max` is unchanged.
- `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` with `max` no longer prefer higher resolution, with
  or without ZSL (see below).

On the Galaxy S21 this gives full-resolution photos with ZSL: 3024x4032, with the
same latency as `high` + ZSL.

### Trade-off to confirm

On devices whose largest photo size is only in the high-resolution list, enabling
ZSL with `max` gives the largest regular size instead. For the device reported in
flutter/packages#11956 that would be 3264x2448 instead of 4624x3468. CameraX does not
allow ZSL with high-resolution sizes.

### Preview and ImageAnalysis

flutter/packages#11956 first applied the high-resolution mode to `ImageCapture` only,
since the original issue was about still capture. At review request it was extended
to `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis`, so that `max` means the highest resolution across
the board.

Keeping it there would keep ZSL off:

- `Preview` cannot be recreated when ZSL is enabled. Recreating it creates a new
  `SurfaceProducer` and so a new texture ID, but that ID was already returned as the
  camera ID, and the camera package only allows enabling ZSL after initialization.
- High-resolution sizes cannot sustain 20 fps (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`), which
  streaming use cases like `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` rely on.

On the Galaxy S21 the `max` preview is 1440x1080 with or without the mode. Is there a
use case that needs high-resolution sizes for `Preview` or `ImageAnalysis`?

title: [web] Safari 27 + minimum font size > 16: typography sentinel line-height factor still mismatches after #186474
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #185931 (fixed by #186474). The same symptom is still reproducible on **Safari 27.2** when Safari's minimum font size is set above 16 *before* the page loads.

The engine's typography sentinel ends up with a clamped `font-size` **and** a proportionally scaled `line-height`, so the expected line-height factor (`9999 / fontSize`) no longer equals the measured ratio (`lineHeight / fontSize`). The engine then treats line-height as overridden and applies a bogus `lineHeightScaleFactorOverride` (~625), which stretches every layout.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.44.8 (stable), engine `0cd610717b` (2026-07-23)
- Safari 27.2 (AppleWebKit 605.1.15), macOS
- Safari → Settings → Advanced → "Never use font sizes smaller than: **19**" (`WebKitMinimumFontSize = 19`), set before load
- `flutter build web --release`, default renderer (CanvasKit)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set "Never use font sizes smaller than" to a value greater than 16, quit and relaunch Safari.
2. Load an app route that lays out a scrollable content column.

## Expected

Normal layout (works in Chromium).

## Actual

The header renders, then remaining widgets are pushed thousands of pixels down inside an enormous scroll view — or the page appears blank. Zooming in/out forces a re-layout that sometimes paints correctly.

## Measurements

Reading the sentinel (`p` with text `flutter typography measurement`) via `getComputedStyle`:

**Broken (minimum font size 19):**

```
font-size:   16.52174px
line-height: 10325.05px
measured ratio:              10325.05 / 16.52174 = 625.0
engine expectation (current): 9999 / 16.52174     = 605.2   <-- mismatch
```

**With the sentinel forced above the clamp:**

```
font-size:   100px
line-height: 9999px
ratio:       99.990 = 9999 / 100   <-- matches, layout renders normally
```

Both values appear to be scaled by the same browser text-scale factor (1.0326 here), while `defaultLineHeightFactor` in `lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/platform_dispatcher.dart` still divides the *unscaled* `9999` by the *scaled* font size.

Effect of the fix on the same page: semantics nodes went from 4 (stretched) to 51, and exposed text from 16 chars (page header only) to 1511 chars (full content).

## Workaround

```css
p[aria-hidden="true"] { font-size: 100px !important; }
```

Placed in `index.html` so it applies before the engine creates/measures the sentinel. This keeps the sentinel above the clamp threshold, so neither value is scaled and the ratios match.

## Notes

- Firestore, CORS and WebGL were ruled out on the same machine: SDK reads return in ~0.5 s, REST reads in ~0.3 s, WebGL2 is available and the home route renders normally.
- Happy to provide a minimal repro app if the existing sample at https://alancook.github.io/patient-manager/safari-test/ is not sufficient.

title: [iOS][UIScene] Plugins receive application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: twice on a cold launch with connection options (background_fetch crashes)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Take an iOS app on Flutter 3.44.1 that has adopted the UIScene lifecycle (`UIApplicationSceneManifest` in Info.plist, `UISceneDelegateClassName` = `FlutterSceneDelegate` or a subclass; plugins registered from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine`).
2. Add a plugin that still uses the application lifecycle (no `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate`) and does something that must happen exactly once in `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`. The real-world case is `background_fetch` (Transistorsoft), which registers its `BGTaskScheduler` launch handler there. A minimal stand-in is a `FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate` that counts calls (see code sample).
3. Terminate the app.
4. Cold-launch it through something that carries **scene connection options**: tap a local/push notification, a Live Activity, a Home Screen quick action, or open a custom URL scheme (`xcrun simctl openurl <udid> myscheme://x` reproduces it on the simulator).

Launching from the app icon (no connection options) does not reproduce.

### Expected results

Plugins receive `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:` once per process, as they do under the classic app-delegate lifecycle.

### Actual results

Plugins receive it **twice** within the same launch:

1. From the storyboard `FlutterViewController` init: `sceneFallbackWillFinishLaunchingApplication:` / `sceneFallbackDidFinishLaunchingApplication:` ([FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324)). This sets `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch = YES` ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129)).
2. Again from `scene:willConnectToSession:options:` when no plugin claims the connection: `FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate` calls `sceneWillConnectFallback:` ([FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270)), which converts the connection options to launch options and calls `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:YES` directly, **without checking `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch`** ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173)). Its own guard (`_sceneWillConnectFallbackCalled`) only prevents a third call; it does not know about the first one.

The only difference between the two deliveries is the `launchOptions` dictionary (empty the first time, the converted connection options the second time), so a plugin cannot tell them apart.

With `background_fetch` the second call ends the process in under a second:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInternalInconsistencyException',
reason: 'Launch handler for task with identifier com.transistorsoft.fetch has already been registered'

-[BGTaskScheduler registerForTaskWithIdentifier:usingQueue:launchHandler:]
-[TSBackgroundFetch registerAppRefreshTask]
-[TSBackgroundFetch didFinishLaunching]
-[BackgroundFetchPlugin application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate sceneWillConnectFallback:]
-[FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:flutterEngine:options:]
-[FlutterSceneDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:options:]
```

Seen in production on iOS 18 through iOS 27 (same engine, so the OS version does not matter); 100% of launches from a Live Activity / notification tap crashed, while icon launches were fine, which is why it passed QA. The code paths above are unchanged on `master` at 7102630 as of 2026-10-27.

Workaround that works for us: register a tiny `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate` through `registrar.addSceneDelegate(...)` whose `scene(_:willConnectTo:options:)` returns `true`. Because a plugin then "handled" the connection, the engine skips `sceneWillConnectFallback:`. That is only acceptable when the app consumes its URL / notification / shortcut itself via the scene delegate; otherwise legacy plugins lose the launch options.

Suggested fix: make `sceneWillConnectFallback:` respect `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch` (or merge the two fallbacks so the converted connection options are passed in the single delivery). Related readability issue: #185705.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

A lifecycle delegate that shows the double delivery without any third-party plugin. Register it from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine` (so it exists before the storyboard `FlutterViewController` is created), then cold-launch via a URL scheme or notification tap.

```swift
final class LaunchCounter: NSObject, FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate {
  private var count = 0
  func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                   didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
    count += 1
    print("didFinishLaunching delivered \(count)x, options: \(launchOptions.keys)")
    precondition(count == 1, "didFinishLaunching delivered twice")   // trips on the second delivery
    return true
  }
}

// in AppDelegate (FlutterAppDelegate subclass, UIScene manifest present)
func didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine(_ engineBridge: FlutterImplicitEngineBridge) {
  GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: engineBridge.pluginRegistry)
  engineBridge.pluginRegistry.registrar(forPlugin: "LaunchCounter")?
    .addApplicationDelegate(LaunchCounter())
}
```

Output on a tap/URL cold launch:

```
didFinishLaunching delivered 1x, options: []
didFinishLaunching delivered 2x, options: [UIApplicationLaunchOptionsKey(_rawValue: UIApplicationLaunchOptionsURLKey), ...]
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console
[!] Flutter (Channel [user-branch], 3.44.1, on macOS 27.0.1 26A434 darwin-arm64, locale en-KR)
    • Framework revision 924134a44c (2026-05-29), engine revision c416acfeb8, Dart 3.12.1, DevTools 2.57.0

Predictive back is modeled as a per-page transition builder, which cannot coordinate route pairs or nested navigators
body:
## Summary

Several issues in Flutter's predictive back support look like isolated edge cases at first glance, but actually stem from the same architectural mismatch:

1. **Unrelated gestures trigger predictive back visuals (#187492):** Dragging a `CupertinoSheet` over a page that uses `PredictiveBackPageTransitionsBuilder` or `PredictiveBackFullscreenPageTransitionsBuilder` causes the underlying page to jump into the predictive back transition and clip its corners. The narrower condition proposed in flutter/packages#12705 still reproduces ([repro comment link](TODO)).
2. **Mixed routes cannot animate together:** When a Material page using a predictive back builder is popped over a `CupertinoPageRoute` (or a custom route), the revealed page remains frozen instead of animating with the predictive back gesture, because the predictive back builders return `null` for `delegatedTransition` and the revealed route does not run the predictive transition itself.
3. **Nested navigators pop the wrong route or pop multiple routes at once (#152323 and its duplicates #183597, #185444):** Swiping back while a root dialog or page covers a nested `Navigator` pops the hidden nested route underneath (#152323); and when both parent and child navigators have active routes, a single back swipe pops both simultaneously (#183597, #185444).

These are not bugs caused by a missing boolean check. They happen because **predictive back is modeled as a per-route `PageTransitionsBuilder` with a per-route global `WidgetsBindingObserver`**, whereas the feature being modeled is a **navigator-level interaction that must follow the same dispatch path as back presses and choreograph a pair of routes**.

## Why these bugs prove the current model is wrong

### 1. A two-page choreography is split across two independent `PageTransitionsBuilder`s
During an Android predictive back gesture, the exiting top page and the revealed page beneath it move as a single coordinated animation. Under the current model, nobody owns that pair: `PageTransitionsBuilder.buildTransitions` runs independently for each route, and each page is responsible for switching its own subtree from its standard transition (`FadeForwards` or `Zoom`) to the predictive transition.

Because the exiting page handles the gesture while the revealed page declines it, **the revealed page has no direct way to know what the page on top is doing.** It is forced to guess by reading indirect signals:
- **`route.popGestureInProgress` is navigator-wide, not route-specific:** Despite its doc comment, it returns `navigator!.userGestureInProgress`, which is true during *any* user gesture on the navigator—including a `CupertinoSheet` drag or an iOS back swipe.
- **Local observer `_phase` goes stale whenever a gesture is declined:** Every `_PredictiveBackGestureDetector` sets `_phase = start` when `handleStartBackGesture` arrives, before checking whether to accept it. Detectors that decline the gesture never receive `commit` or `cancel`, leaving `_phase` stuck at `start` indefinitely.

Any attempt to fix this while keeping per-route inference runs into a wall:
- **Only setting `_phase` when accepting** breaks the revealed page, which declines the gesture and would never enter the predictive transition. Moreover, `WidgetsBindingObserver`s run in registration order, so the revealed page receives `handleStartBackGesture` *before* the top page even decides whether to accept it.
- **Scoping `popGestureInProgress` to the route directly above** still fails because dragging a `CupertinoSheet` *is* that sheet route's pop gesture—and existing consumers like `CupertinoPageTransitionsBuilder` rely on `popGestureInProgress` being navigator-wide.
- **Wiring a detector into `delegatedTransition` (in-flight PR #174337)** still relies on the same per-route inference: the revealed route wraps itself in its own detector and checks `_phase` and `route?.popGestureInProgress` to guess whether a predictive back gesture is underway, while `delegatedTransition` itself is wired up when the route stack changes rather than per gesture and receives the revealed route's animations rather than the top route's state.
- **Broadcasting a navigator-level "predictive back in progress" flag** only works when both routes understand the broadcast. If a Material page is popped to reveal a `CupertinoPageRoute` or custom route that doesn't read the flag, the revealed route still cannot participate properly.

### 2. Gesture dispatch is split from back-press dispatch and bypasses the `Navigator` hierarchy
On Android (`OnBackInvokedDispatcher` / `OnBackPressedDispatcher`), a discrete back button press and a continuous predictive back gesture are routed through the same dispatcher: a single active callback is selected at start time based on priority and enabled state, and only that callback receives the gesture lifecycle (`started` -> `progressed` -> `committed`/`cancelled`).

In Flutter, discrete back presses go through `handlePopRoute` -> `WidgetsApp` / `Router` -> root `Navigator.maybePop`, delegating to nested navigators only when explicitly forwarded via `NavigatorPopHandler` or `ChildBackButtonDispatcher`. Predictive back gestures ignore that path completely. Because `_PredictiveBackGestureDetector` lives inside `PageTransitionsBuilder`, every page registers its own global `WidgetsBindingObserver` and checks `route.isCurrent && route.popGestureEnabled` in isolation:
- `route.isCurrent` only means "on top of my own `Navigator`". A route inside a nested `Navigator` has no idea that its enclosing route in the root `Navigator` is covered by a `Dialog` or another page (#152323).
- Since #154718, `WidgetsBinding` sends `update` and `commit` to *every* observer that returns `true` from `handleStartBackGesture` (contradicting the method's doc comment). When both a parent and child navigator have `isCurrent` routes with predictive back builders (and the parent is not blocked by a `PopScope`), both accept the gesture and both pop (#152323, #183597, #185444).

### 3. Forward transitions and predictive back transitions are artificially coupled
Embedding predictive back inside `PageTransitionsBuilder` forces apps to pick a builder (`PredictiveBackPageTransitionsBuilder` or `PredictiveBackFullscreenPageTransitionsBuilder`) that hardcodes a specific forward transition (`FadeForwards` or `Zoom`), and leaves `CupertinoPageRoute` unable to participate in predictive back on Android at all.

## Requirements that any replacement model must meet

To fix these issues at the root rather than trading one edge case for another, the model needs to satisfy:

1. **Unified, single-target dispatch aligned with back presses:** At most one `Navigator` and one `Route` may handle a system back gesture, chosen at gesture start using the same hierarchy and explicit forwarding rules (`NavigatorPopHandler` / `BackButtonDispatcher`) as standard back presses (#152323).
2. **Single-owner two-page choreography:** Within the handling navigator, the exiting route must drive both its own exit transition and the revealed route's entrance transition during a predictive back gesture—without the revealed route inspecting gesture signals, and regardless of what `PageTransitionsBuilder` or `ModalRoute` subclass the revealed page uses (#187492).
3. **Gesture isolation until settle:** Predictive back visuals must trigger *only* for accepted system back gestures (never for sheet drags or iOS back swipes), and must remain active after `commit` or `cancel` until the route's settle animation finishes.
4. **Surface-specific participation:** A route being popped must be able to choose whether to use the two-page predictive transition (standard pages), drive its own primary animation directly (e.g., container transforms), or opt out (e.g., dialogs and sheets).
5. **Decoupling from forward transitions and `material_ui`:** Predictive back configuration should be independent of the forward `PageTransitionsBuilder` and live at the `widgets` layer so `CupertinoPageRoute` and custom `ModalRoute`s can participate on Android.
6. **Backward compatibility:** Existing `PageTransitionsBuilder`s, custom `Route` subclasses, and `go_router` setups must keep working without breaking changes unless an app opts in.

*(See the follow-up comment for a concrete design sketch and incremental migration path.)*

body:
### Description

Building `flutter_tools` on `master` fails to compile at commit https://github.com/flutter/flutter/commit/6da6a9b8dd29984bb563ff8e891257b4126078b3 (#193652):

```text
Building flutter tool...
Got dependencies.
flutter/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/macos/build_macos.dart:234:16: Error: Undefined name 'globals'.
    cocoaPods: globals.cocoaPods,
               ^^^^^^^
flutter/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/macos/build_macos.dart:235:23: Error: Undefined name 'globals'.
    templateRenderer: globals.templateRenderer,
```

### Root Cause

Semantic merge conflict in `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/macos/build_macos.dart` between two PRs:
1. #194052 (`335c5568222c`) added `cocoaPods: globals.cocoaPods` and `templateRenderer: globals.templateRenderer` to the `processPodsIfNeeded` call in `build_macos.dart`.
2. #193652 (`6da6a9b8dd29`) removed `import '../globals.dart' as globals;` from `build_macos.dart` without updating those two parameters to use the injected `cocoaPods` / `toolContext.templateRenderer`.

We are facing an issue while upgrading to the latest Flutter SDK on Windows machines.
Our organization works in a restricted banking network environment, and due to security policies, PowerShell access is completely blocked for all employees.

The latest Flutter SDK on Windows requires PowerShell to run critical setup commands (including flutter doctor, flutter upgrade, SDK initialization scripts etc.). Since PowerShell is mandatory, the SDK upgrade does not proceed and errors are thrown.

As we cannot enable PowerShell due to strict banking security policies, we are completely unable to update Flutter SDK to the latest stable release.

**Environment Details**
OS: Windows (Enterprise / Banking Restricted Environment)
PowerShell: Not available (blocked by IT security policy)
Terminal availability: Only CMD is allowed
Flutter version: Older version (works fine without PowerShell)
Need: A way to upgrade Flutter SDK without requiring PowerShell, or an alternative shell compatibility option.

Run a Flutter application on a Windows PC equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 5 125H or Intel Core Ultra 7 155H processor and its integrated GPU.

Monitor the application's memory usage in Windows Task Manager while it is running.

Run the same Flutter application on systems equipped with an NVIDIA discrete GPU, an older Intel integrated GPU, and an Intel Arc B580 discrete GPU, and compare the memory usage.

### Expected results

Memory usage should remain within a reasonable range when running the same Flutter application under similar conditions across different GPU configurations. There should not be a significant unexplained difference in memory usage on specific integrated GPUs.

On systems equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 5 125H or Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, running a Flutter application with the integrated GPU results in relatively high memory usage, reaching several hundred megabytes.

In comparison, I have not observed the same issue on systems equipped with an NVIDIA discrete GPU, an older Intel integrated GPU, or an Intel Arc B580 discrete GPU.

Use the app normally: navigate between screens and add several entries to a list, so a lot of new text is drawn. 3. After a while, every glyph drawn by Flutter becomes corrupted. We don't have a minimal reproduction yet. The device belongs to an end user. ### Expected results Text renders normally. ### Actual results Every glyph Flutter draws (app bar title, tabs, list text, dialog text, button labels, and Material icon-font icons in the bottom navigation bar) shows as broken, misaligned fragments of glyphs. It looks like the glyph atlas is being sampled with wrong coordinates or holds corrupted data. The Android system UI (status bar) on the same screen renders correctly, so the corruption is limited to Flutter's rendering. We have only seen this on this device. No custom fonts are bundled; the app uses the default Roboto / Material Icons. ### Screenshot ### Device | | | |---|---| | Device | Samsung Galaxy A41 (SM-A415F) | | SoC / GPU | MediaTek Helio P65 (MT6768) / Arm Mali-G52 MC2 | | Android version | Android 12 (API 31) | | Impeller backend | Vulkan (inferred, not confirmed from logs) | Why we infer Vulkan: on 3.38.7, `GetActualRenderingAPIForImpeller` only forces OpenGLES on MediaTek below API 31, and the A41 runs API 31. In 3.47.x the threshold moved to `ro.vendor.build.version.sdk < 32`, which would put this device on OpenGLES. So this may already be avoided on newer versions, but only by that MediaTek fallback and not by a fix to the underlying bug. ### Flutter version Flutter 3.38.7 (stable), Dart 3.10.7. Release build.
