title: [Linux] DEBUG_PRINT_LAYOUT is left on in fl_keyboard_manager.cc; its loop looks up keycodes 0-7 and crashes on an X display without XKB (ssh -X)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

On Linux, a Flutter app segfaults on its first key press when it runs as an untrusted X client, for example over `ssh -X` with OpenSSH's default `ForwardX11Trusted no` (the default on macOS). The same app works as a trusted client (`ssh -Y`).

Minimal repro on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04, Flutter 3.47.7 stable:

1. `flutter create --platforms=linux app`
2. In `linux/runner/my_application.cc`, call `fl_dart_project_set_enable_impeller(project, FALSE);` (so the software renderer works under Xvfb).
3. `flutter build linux --release`
4. Start an X server with the SECURITY extension and make an untrusted cookie:
   ```
   xauth -f t add :77 . $(mcookie)
   Xvfb :77 -auth t +extension SECURITY -noreset &
   XAUTHORITY=t xauth -f u generate :77 . untrusted timeout 3600
   ```
5. Run the app as the untrusted client and type one key as a trusted one:
   ```
   DISPLAY=:77 XAUTHORITY=u FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software build/linux/x64/release/bundle/app &
   DISPLAY=:77 XAUTHORITY=t xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --name app windowfocus --sync
   DISPLAY=:77 XAUTHORITY=t xdotool type a
   ```

### Expected results

The key press reaches the app, as it does with `XAUTHORITY=t` (a trusted client).

### Actual results

The app is killed by SIGSEGV in `gdk_x11_keymap_lookup_key`.

Cause: `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_keyboard_manager.cc` line 19 has `#define DEBUG_PRINT_LAYOUT`, which has been on since flutter/engine#32665 (April 2022) and is still on in master. With it on, `guarantee_layout()` runs `for (uint16_t keycode = 0; keycode < 128; keycode += 1)`, calling `convert_key_to_char` and so `gdk_keymap_lookup_key()` for keycodes 0 to 127 on the first key press of each group. It builds `debug_layout_data`, which is never printed.

X keycodes start at the display's `min_keycode` (8 here). With XKEYBOARD, GDK tolerates keycode 0. An untrusted client is not given XKEYBOARD, so GDK uses the core keymap, computes `(0 - min_keycode)` unsigned, and reads out of bounds.

Suggested fix: remove the `#define` (or make it opt-in). Optionally, `convert_key_to_char` could also skip keycodes outside the display's `XDisplayKeycodes` range.

### Code sample

The stock `flutter create` app, with only the Impeller change in step 2.

### Logs

Stack, Ubuntu 24.04, GTK 3.24.41-4ubuntu1.3, gdb with debuginfod:

```
#0  gdk_x11_keymap_lookup_key (keymap=GdkX11Keymap, key=0x7fffffffc840) at gdk/x11/gdkkeys-x11.c:1063
#1  libflutter_linux_gtk.so (guarantee_layout / convert_key_to_char, inlined)
#2  libflutter_linux_gtk.so (fl_keyboard_manager_handle_event path)
#3-#7  g_signal_emit key-press-event on FlView
#8  gtk_widget_event_internal (FlView)
#9  gtk_window_propagate_key_event
#10 gtk_window_key_press_event
#16-#19 gtk_widget_event_internal / propagate_event / gtk_main_do_event
#21 _gdk_event_emit
#23 gdk_event_source_dispatch
#24-#28 g_main_context_iteration / g_application_run
#29 main
```

At the crash: `*key = {keycode = 0, group = 0, level = 0}`, keymap `min_keycode = 8`, `max_keycode = 255`, `keysyms_per_keycode = 7`, `xkb_desc = NULL`, `rax = 0xffffffc8` (that is `(0 - 8) * 7`). A breakpoint on `gdk_keymap_lookup_key` counts 354 calls on the first key: keycodes 0 to 127 at levels 0 and 1 (the debug loop) plus the 49 layout goals. The same crash happens on Ubuntu 22.04 (GTK 3.24.33).

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.47.7 stable, engine d8a2d6c768, on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 (GitHub Actions runners).

title: [iOS] Flutter content painted after a non-rect-clipped platform view disappears when another platform view covers the background canvas
[web][a11y] Desktop: a screen reader reading forward never reaches the "Enable accessibility" placeholder, and Tab reaches it last
body:
### Steps to reproduce

A screen reader user has to activate the "Enable accessibility" placeholder before a Flutter web app exposes any content at all. On desktop that placeholder is prepended to `<body>`, ahead of `<flutter-view>`, and `ViewFocusBinding` focuses the view at startup — so reading forward from where the page leaves you never arrives at it. The engine's own comment says the placeholder's `aria-live` region announces it "as soon as the page receives focus" and that `tabindex` "makes sure the button is the first target of tab"; measured on a stock app, neither holds. The live region has no content to announce, and Tab reaches the placeholder only after a full cycle out through the browser chrome.

The first two steps need nothing but a browser and VoiceOver. Steps 3 and 4 are the DOM evidence for why.

**1.** `flutter create repro && cd repro` — no edits. Then `flutter run -d web-server --web-port 4300` and open `http://127.0.0.1:4300` in Chrome on macOS.

**2.** Once it has painted, **do not click in the page**, and turn VoiceOver on with Cmd+F5. Press **VO+Right** a dozen or more times to read forward, then **VO+Left** once.

Keep the placeholder out of the keyboard's way while doing this. Any non-Tab key event whose target is the placeholder enables semantics and removes it — including the Shift **keyup** that ends a Shift+Tab, so Shift+Tab onto it destroys the state you are trying to observe. Plain forward Tab does not. Once semantics are on, none of this is observable until a reload; the readout in step 4 reports `semanticsNodes`, which must stay `0`.

**3.** Reload, leave semantics off, and run this in the console to see where the placeholder sits and what it carries:

```js
const fv = document.querySelector('flutter-view');
const ph = document.querySelector('flt-semantics-placeholder');
({
  activeIsFlutterView: document.activeElement === fv,
  placeholderIsBodyFirstChild: document.body.firstElementChild === ph,
  placeholderPrecedesView: !!(ph.compareDocumentPosition(fv) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING),
  flutterViewRole: fv.getAttribute('role'),
  flutterViewAriaLabel: fv.getAttribute('aria-label'),
  placeholderRole: ph.getAttribute('role'),
  placeholderTabindex: ph.getAttribute('tabindex'),
  placeholderAriaLive: ph.getAttribute('aria-live'),
  placeholderAriaLabel: ph.getAttribute('aria-label'),
  placeholderTextContent: JSON.stringify(ph.textContent),
  placeholderChildCount: ph.childNodes.length,
})
```

**4.** Optional, for the Tab behaviour. Reading `document.hasFocus()` *from the console* does not work — clicking into DevTools takes focus out of the page, so it reports `false` for that reason alone. Paste this once for a live readout on the page instead, then close DevTools and leave it closed:

```js
(() => {
  if (window.__probeTimer) { clearInterval(window.__probeTimer); window.__probeEl?.remove(); }
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;z-index:99999;top:0;right:0;background:#000;color:#0f0;font:13px/1.4 monospace;padding:8px;white-space:pre;pointer-events:none';
  document.body.appendChild(el);
  window.__probeEl = el;
  window.__probeTimer = setInterval(() => {
    const ph = document.querySelector('flt-semantics-placeholder');
    const ae = document.activeElement;
    el.textContent =
      'activeElement   : ' + (ae ? ae.tagName.toLowerCase() : 'null') +
      '\nhasFocus        : ' + document.hasFocus() +
      '\nisPlaceholder   : ' + (ae === ph) +
      '\nplaceholderInDom: ' + !!ph +
      '\nsemanticsNodes  : ' + document.querySelectorAll('flt-semantics').length;
  }, 100);
})();
```

With DevTools closed, press **Tab** repeatedly and watch the readout — keep going past the point where focus leaves the page, on through the address bar and the browser's other controls, until it re-enters the page. The div is appended, so `body.firstElementChild` is still the placeholder and the tab order is unchanged. `semanticsNodes` stays at `0` while semantics are off; if it is not `0`, the placeholder has already been activated — reload and start again.


### Expected results

Moving forward through a freshly loaded page — by Tab, or by reading with a screen reader — reaches the "Enable accessibility" placeholder, since it is the control that makes everything else accessible.


### Actual results

The step 3 snippet returns, on an unmodified `flutter create` app:

```
activeIsFlutterView:          true
placeholderIsBodyFirstChild:  true
placeholderPrecedesView:      true
flutterViewRole:              null
flutterViewAriaLabel:         null
placeholderRole:             "button"
placeholderTabindex:         "0"
placeholderAriaLive:         "polite"
placeholderAriaLabel:        "Enable accessibility"
placeholderTextContent:      ""
placeholderChildCount:        0
```

**Reading forward never reaches it.** With VoiceOver (Chrome, macOS, Polish UI), VO+Right announces "grupa" — "group", the unnamed `<flutter-view>` — and keeps announcing it however many times it is pressed. Tried about fifteen times: forward reading never advances past that one element and never wraps round the way Tab does. VO+Left, from any point, announces "Enable accessibility" immediately.

**The live region never announces it.** `aria-live="polite"` announces *changes to a region's content*. This element has no content: `textContent` is `""` and `childNodes.length` is `0`, because the message is in `aria-label`, which a live region does not watch. Both are set in `_prepareAccessibilityPlaceholder` before the element is inserted, so there is no post-insertion change either.

**Tab reaches it last, not first.** From the startup focus, Tab steps through the app's own focusables and then leaves the document for the browser chrome. On the stock counter app the first Tab goes to the `FloatingActionButton` — DOM `activeElement` stays `<flutter-view>`, since with semantics off the framework handles focus internally — and the second leaves the document (`document.hasFocus()` becomes `false`). On a variant with nothing focusable at all, the *first* Tab leaves the document.

The placeholder is reached eventually: keep tabbing through the address bar and the browser's other controls, and focus re-enters the page at the top, where the placeholder is the first tabbable element in document order. So it is reachable, but as the furthest point of a full round trip through the browser UI rather than the first stop. Going the other way is far shorter: two Shift+Tab presses land on it, the first consumed by the `FloatingActionButton` exactly as forward Tab is.

**What does reach it.** One VO+Left press, two Shift+Tab presses, forward Tab after a cycle through the browser chrome, and the rotor's Form Controls list — so the placeholder is not unreachable, and this report does not claim it is.

What fails is discovery for someone who does not already know it is there. They hear one unnamed "group" and nothing else, so nothing suggests reversing, opening the rotor, or tabbing on through the address bar. The two routes the engine documents — announce on load, first target of Tab — are the ones meant for that user, and neither holds on a stock app.

## Why it happens

**The placeholder is before the view.** On 3.47.4, unconditionally in `EnginePlatformDispatcher`'s constructor — `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/platform_dispatcher.dart:40`, `domDocument.body?.prepend(accessibilityPlaceholder)`. On master it moved into `SemanticsEnabler.addPlaceholderForView`, where the host is per form factor — desktop `domDocument.body`, mobile `viewRoot` — so the desktop DOM position is unchanged. (Read on master, not run.)

**The view takes focus at startup.** `ViewFocusBinding` calls `viewElement?.focusWithoutScroll()` when the framework requests view focus (`view_focus_binding.dart:48` on 3.47.4, `:70` on master). On a stock app this has happened by first paint — measured by patching `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` before `main.dart.js` loads: exactly one call, on `<flutter-view>`, no application frame in the stack, roughly 0.7–1.9 s after load in debug and 130–200 ms in release.

**The engine names two discovery mechanisms, and the repro contradicts both.** `_prepareAccessibilityPlaceholder` says, identically on 3.47.4 (`semantics_helper.dart:200-204`) and master:

```dart
// Adding roles to semantics placeholder. 'aria-live' will make sure that
// the content is announced to the assistive technology user as soon as the
// page receives focus. 'tabindex' makes sure the button is the first
// target of tab. 'aria-label' is used to define the placeholder message
// to the assistive technology user.
```

The live region announces nothing, because the element it is on has no content. And the placeholder is not the first target of Tab but the last, because Tab starts from the view rather than from the top of the document, and only comes back round to the placeholder after leaving the page entirely.

The placement itself is deliberate: `DesktopSemanticsEnabler.placeholderHostFor`'s doc comment says the placeholder "has to be the first thing the user tabs to", since once focus enters a view Flutter's traversal can consume Tab and never hand it back. Hosting it in `body` is the right answer to that — but only while Tab starts at the top, and the startup focus means it does not. Step 4 measures the situation that comment warns about, on an app that opted into nothing.

Separately, `<flutter-view>` has a `tabindex` (`view_focus_binding.dart:143`) but no `role` and no `aria-label`, which is why the landing announcement is a bare "group". That is a different defect: naming the view would fix the announcement without moving the placeholder in front of anyone.

Reported on 3.47.4. The files cited here — `platform_dispatcher.dart`, `platform_dispatcher/view_focus_binding.dart`, `semantics/semantics_helper.dart` — are byte-identical between tags `3.47.4` and `3.47.8`, so current stable behaves the same. Scope is desktop; on 3.47.4 the prepend to `body` is unconditional so mobile browsers share the DOM position, and from 3.50 (currently in beta; newest stable is 3.47.8) they do not.


### Code sample

An unmodified `flutter create` app reproduces this — the counter app's own `FloatingActionButton` is the only focusable widget. The variant below removes even that, so the first Tab leaves the document immediately rather than being consumed by the button; both behave the same with respect to the placeholder.

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// Nothing focusable anywhere: no FAB, no buttons, no text fields.
void main() => runApp(
  const MaterialApp(
    home: Scaffold(body: Center(child: Text('nothing focusable here'))),
  ),
);
```

</details>


### Screenshots or Video

Stock `flutter create` app on 3.47.4, Chrome on macOS, VoiceOver with the caption panel on. Nothing in the page is clicked at any point, so semantics stay off and the placeholder is never activated.

VO+Right is pressed repeatedly: each press announces "grupa" — Polish for "group", the unnamed `<flutter-view>` — and reading never advances past it. A single VO+Left then announces "Enable accessibility".

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31599d01-4385-4662-a838-188a3ac01ba5

</details>


### Logs

_No response_

title: vector_graphics_compiler: widen the xml bound to admit xml 7.1.0
body:
## The ask

Please widen `vector_graphics_compiler`'s `xml` dependency from `xml >=6.3.0 <=7.0.1` to a caret that admits `xml` 7.1.0 (e.g. `xml: ">=6.3.0 <8.0.0"` or `^7.1.0` with the floor you support).

## Why

xml 7.1.0 is a normal semver-compatible release on the 7.x line, but the tight upper bound (`<=7.0.1`) makes it unsolvable for any app that needs xml 7.1.0 while depending on `flutter_svg` (which drags this package in transitively):

```
Because vector_graphics_compiler >=1.2.5 depends on xml >=6.3.0 <=7.0.1, vector_graphics_compiler >=1.1.12 requires xml >=6.3.0 <=7.0.1.
And because flutter_svg >=2.3.0 requires vector_graphics_compiler ^1.1.14, flutter_svg >=2.3.0 requires xml >=6.3.0 <=7.0.1.
So, because zik_zak depends on both flutter_svg ^2.3.0 and xml ^7.1.0, version solving failed.
```

Our app carries `dependency_overrides: xml: ^7.1.0` purely to bypass this one bound — every other package in our graph (including our own published packages, e.g. a maintained minio fork) is on xml ^7.1.0 and works, so there is no known API break from 7.0.1 → 7.1.0 that would justify the cap.

## Environment

- vector_graphics_compiler 1.3.4 (latest), flutter_svg 2.3.2, Flutter 3.47.7 stable, Dart 3.12
- Resolver output above is from `flutter pub get` on 2026-10-29

title: [Flutter GPU][iOS] `gpuContext.defaultColorFormat` is `PixelFormat.unknown` on wide-gamut devices once the first frame is rasterized
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On a device that supports wide gamut (we used an iPhone 13 mini), with the default `FLTEnableWideGamut` (not set in `Info.plist`), run the code sample below with `flutter run --profile`.
2. Read the two printed lines, then the exception.

### Expected results

`defaultColorFormat` is documented as "a supported [PixelFormat] for textures that store 4-channel colors". It should stay a format that `createTexture` accepts, for example `b8g8r8a8UNormInt`, as it is before the first frame.

### Actual results

Before the first frame, `defaultColorFormat` is usually `b8g8r8a8UNormInt`. After the first rasterized frame it is `PixelFormat.unknown`, and `createTexture` with it fails:

```
before: PixelFormat.b8g8r8a8UNormInt
after: PixelFormat.unknown
[ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/metal/allocator_mtl.mm(171)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Texture descriptor was invalid.
[ERROR:flutter/lib/gpu/texture.cc(253)] Failed to create texture.
[ERROR:flutter/runtime/dart_vm_initializer.cc(40)] Unhandled Exception: Exception: Texture creation failed
```

What we measured, logging `defaultColorFormat` before the first frame, right after `waitUntilFirstFrameRasterized`, and 2 s after the first frame:

| `FLTEnableWideGamut` | launches | before first frame | after first frame | 2 s later |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| not set (default) | 4 | `b8g8r8a8UNormInt` in 3, `unknown` in 1 | `unknown` in 4 | `unknown` in 4 |
| `false` | 3 | `b8g8r8a8UNormInt` | `b8g8r8a8UNormInt` | `b8g8r8a8UNormInt` |

So code that creates textures early usually works and sometimes fails, and code that creates them after the first frame always fails.

As far as we can read the source (engine `5f77625673`):

- `FlutterDartProject.mm`: wide gamut is enabled by default on hardware that supports it.
- `FlutterView.mm`, `layoutSubviews`: with wide gamut, the layer's `pixelFormat` becomes `MTLPixelFormatBGRA10_XR`.
- `ios_surface_metal_impeller.mm`, `CreateGPUSurface`: calls `UpdateOffscreenLayerPixelFormat` with that format, and `ContextMTL::UpdateOffscreenLayerPixelFormat` rebuilds the capabilities with it as the default color format (`kB10G10R10A10XR`).
- `lib/gpu/formats.h`: `kB10G10R10XR`, `kB10G10R10XRSRGB` and `kB10G10R10A10XR` map to `FlutterGPUPixelFormat::kUnknown` ("Apple-only extended-range formats, not exposed by the Flutter GPU API").

Possible directions: have `defaultColorFormat` return a Flutter GPU format when the context's default is one of the XR formats (e.g. `b8g8r8a8UNormInt`), or expose the XR formats in Flutter GPU.

Workaround: pass an explicit format such as `PixelFormat.r8g8b8a8UNormInt`, or set `FLTEnableWideGamut` to `false`.

### Code sample

Condensed from a logging variant of the app attached to #195668 (which itself uses an explicit format). The table above comes from that variant; this snippet in exactly this form has not been run.

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:flutter_gpu/gpu.dart' as gpu;

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  runApp(const SizedBox.expand());
  debugPrint('before: ${gpu.gpuContext.defaultColorFormat}');
  await WidgetsBinding.instance.waitUntilFirstFrameRasterized;
  debugPrint('after: ${gpu.gpuContext.defaultColorFormat}');
  gpu.gpuContext.createTexture(
    gpu.StorageMode.devicePrivate,
    256,
    256,
    format: gpu.gpuContext.defaultColorFormat,
    enableRenderTargetUsage: true,
  );
}
```

### Flutter Doctor output

```
Flutter 3.47.0 • channel stable • https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git
Framework • revision 4cf2416426 • 2026-08-11
Engine • hash 59d54a2b2896a6bbf356c94b7fac7b9e235bdacd (revision 5f77625673)
Tools • Dart 3.13.0 • DevTools 2.60.0
```

title: [Impeller][Vulkan] Flutter GPU `CommandBuffer.submit()` blocks the UI thread while the raster thread is in `vkQueuePresentKHR`
body:
[flutter_gpu_present_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34170930/flutter_gpu_present_repro.zip)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Unpack `flutter_gpu_present_repro.zip`, attached at the top of this issue. It is a single-file app that uses only the SDK's `flutter_gpu` package, with its shader bundle checked in.
2. `flutter run --profile` on an Android device with Impeller Vulkan. We used a Samsung Galaxy A55 (SM-A556E, Exynos 1480 / Xclipse 530, Android 16).
3. Tap the screen to double the fragment-shader load until the frame is GPU-bound, e.g. 1024 iterations at 1024×1024. Then watch the `repro:` lines in logcat.

Each frame, the app renders a heavy full-screen pass into one texture of a ring of three and calls `commandBuffer.submit()`, timing only that call. It then shows the texture through `asImage()` and `RawImage`. A 4 ms `Timer.periodic` measures event-loop stalls.

### Expected results

`submit()` should return quickly, or at least should not hold the UI isolate for most of the frame. It returns quickly on iOS/Metal under the same GPU-bound load.

### Actual results

Once the frame is GPU-bound, the UI thread spends most of every frame inside `submit()`. The whole UI isolate stalls with it, timers and input handling included (on Android the platform and UI threads are merged). Samsung A55, Vulkan:

| iterations | fps | submit median, ms | submit max, ms | timer late max, ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–64 | 120 | 0.4 | ≤ 2.6 | ≤ 7.2 |
| 256 | 63 | 6.3 | 25.9 | 26.9 |
| 1024 | 18 | 39.9 | 47.6 | 51.5 |
| 2048 | 9.5 | 87.8 | 94.7 | 98.3 |

iPhone 13 mini (Metal), same app at 1024 iterations: 13–18 fps, `submit()` under 0.05 ms in every frame, and the watchdog never more than 5.8 ms late.

A systrace at 1024 iterations (in the archive, with `tool/analyze_trace.py`) shows the wait. Over 6.1 s, every long UI-thread sleep (112 of 112, median 37.5 ms, 4.2 s in total) starts while the raster thread is inside `QueuePresentKHR`. The raster thread ends each sleep by waking the UI thread 0.01 ms after that present returns, and the UI thread calls `vkQueueSubmit` within 0.5 ms of waking. The present itself blocks in the driver (`queueBuffer` → `waitForever`).

As far as we can read the source (engine `5f77625673`):

- `lib/gpu/command_buffer.cc`: on Vulkan, `CommandBuffer::Submit` encodes and submits synchronously on the calling (UI) thread. Only GLES posts to the raster thread.
- `CommandQueueVK::Submit` → `FenceWaiterVK::AddFence` (holding `wait_set_mutex_`) → `QueueVK::Submit`, which takes `queue_mutex_`.
- `KHRSwapchainImplVK::Present` → `QueueVK::Present` holds the same `queue_mutex_` for the whole of `vkQueuePresentKHR` (FIFO swapchain).

The lock itself is required, because Vulkan requires external synchronisation of the queue. The cost comes from holding it across a present that can block for tens of milliseconds, while a Flutter GPU submit on the UI thread needs the same lock. Possible directions, for whoever knows the constraints better: submit Flutter GPU work from the raster thread on Vulkan too, as GLES already does; or avoid holding `queue_mutex_` for the full duration of a blocking present (e.g. a separate present queue where available).

### Code sample

`flutter_gpu_present_repro.zip` (attached at the top): `lib/main.dart`, about 200 lines.

### Logs

title: [Windows][a11y] Release access violation in HitTestSync; child delegate lookup lacks null guard
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Not isolated yet. One Windows x64 Release crash was observed in production; there is no known triggering UI action or minimal Flutter sample. A deterministic reproduction has not been identified.

### Expected results

An accessibility hit test should not terminate the process when a child platform delegate is unavailable.

### Actual results and crash report

The app terminated with an unhandled native access violation. The relevant fields from its crash collector are:

```text
exceptionCode: 0xc0000005
frame[0]: flutter_windows.dll + 0xfffa
imageSize: 21446656 (0x1474000)
imageTimestamp: 0
pdbId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
pdbAge: 0
```

The zeros above mean the old collector failed to capture binary identity; they are not the DLL's actual PE/PDB values. This report has no faulting memory address, full native stack, WER minidump, or Dart exception.

A retained local Release DLL has the same `SizeOfImage`. Its PDB maps RVA `0xfffa` to `flutter::FlutterPlatformNodeDelegateWindows::HitTestSync` at `flutter_platform_node_delegate_windows.cc:69`. This symbolization is **provisional** because the report cannot prove that the affected machine loaded that exact DLL.

### Relevant Flutter code

[The current Windows engine source](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/windows/flutter_platform_node_delegate_windows.cc#L64-L71) calls `lock()` on the child delegate's weak pointer, checks it with `FML_DCHECK`, then dereferences it in `win_delegate->HitTestSync(...)`. That check does not guard a null delegate in Release. An expired delegate is a plausible cause, but this report cannot establish the lifetime sequence.

This is the native crash path reported in #192180. The related framework fix #193372 for #190357 does not modify this engine lookup. Could maintainers confirm the delegate-lifetime invariant and whether this lookup needs a runtime guard and regression test?

### Flutter diagnostics

`flutter doctor -v` from the **affected machine** is unavailable. Relevant excerpt from the **build machine** (not the crash environment):

title: LicensePage: the loading state overflows on a landscape phone at large text
[Android] SurfaceHolderCallbackCompat waits for the first frame with no time limit, so a key press ANRs on Android 13
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create bug` and replace `lib/main.dart` with the sample below. It holds frames back for 30 s after the app is left, standing in for a slow first frame.
2. Run it in release mode on an Android 13 (API 33) emulator.
3. Press Home, wait about 8 s, then open the app again.
4. Press Back straight away (`adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_BACK`).

### Expected results

The window shows once Android stops waiting for Flutter, and Back is handled. Android 14 and up do this on their own: `SurfaceSyncGroup` gives up after 1 s (3 s on emulators). The same steps on an Android 17 emulator give no ANR.

### Actual results

The window stays `DRAW_PENDING`, so it can't take focus. The app looks fine, since Android shows its last snapshot, but Back ANRs 5 s later: `Input dispatching timed out (Application does not have a focused window)`.

Since #171398, [`SurfaceHolderCallbackCompat.surfaceRedrawNeededAsync`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/189a5db70ba4f7a652e3349e922ab38a3bca023e/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/android/SurfaceHolderCallbackCompat.java#L141-L165) holds Android's `finishDrawing` until `onFlutterUiDisplayed`, with no limit, and never runs it when `flutterRenderer` is null. Android 13 has no timeout of its own there. Before #171398, Android didn't wait at all.

We hit this in production as a "No focused window" ANR on a Datalogic Memor 12 (Android 13), right after the app came back from the background. What delays the frame on that device is still unknown.

**Suggested fix:** run `finishDrawing` once, on `onFlutterUiDisplayed` or after 1 s, whichever comes first, and straight away when there's no renderer. We ship that as an app-side wrapper for now. Happy to send a PR.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

/// Keeps frames off the screen for 30 s after the app is left, so the first frame after
/// coming back is late.
class LateFrameBinding extends WidgetsFlutterBinding {
  bool _holding = false;

  @override
  bool get sendFramesToEngine => !_holding && super.sendFramesToEngine;

  @override
  void handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(AppLifecycleState state) {
    super.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(state);
    if (state != AppLifecycleState.hidden) return;
    _holding = true;
    Timer(const Duration(seconds: 30), () {
      _holding = false;
      scheduleForcedFrame();
    });
  }
}

void main() {
  LateFrameBinding();
  runApp(
    const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(child: Text('Press Home, come back, press Back')),
      ),
    ),
  );
}
```

</details>

[Impeller][Android][Adreno] Scudo abort in ApplyApplicationProfile during Vulkan initialization (3.47.8 / Shorebird; possible recurrence of #168665)
body:
Related closed report: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/168665

### Summary

We observed a production SIGABRT on a Samsung Galaxy S22 (`SM-S901N`, Android 14) while Impeller creates its Vulkan context. The abort is raised by Scudo during deallocation inside `libadreno_app_profiles.so`, reached through `ApplyApplicationProfile` and Vulkan instance creation.

This is a **possible recurrence of the Scudo stack reported in #168665**, not a confirmed regression. The first 13 system/vendor `(library, PC)` pairs in our Google Play trace match that issue's Scudo trace, including the profile function at `0x37ef8`, `ApplyApplicationProfile+444`, the four Adreno Vulkan PCs, and both Android Vulkan-loader PCs. The Flutter engine itself differs.

We are filing separately because #168665 was closed as a duplicate of #166410, while our failure is in Vulkan initialization / vendor profile deallocation, rather than the animated-image teardown reproduction. We cannot establish whether the original memory-corruption cause is the same.

### Steps to reproduce

This is a production-only observation from Google Play Android vitals, also correlated with a Crashlytics capture by device, OS, version, hour and native PCs. We do **not** have a deterministic local reproduction or a minimal runnable example.

The captured engine call chain is:

```text
Shell::CreateShellOnPlatformThread
  -> PlatformViewAndroid::SetupImpellerContext
  -> AndroidContextDynamicImpeller::SetupImpellerContext
  -> AndroidContextVKImpeller
  -> impeller::ContextVK::Setup
  -> vkCreateInstance
  -> qglinternal::vkEnumerateInstanceVersion
  -> ApplyApplicationProfile
  -> vendor profile function
  -> scudo::Allocator::deallocate
  -> scudo::reportInvalidChunkState
  -> abort
```

We cannot determine whether this was the initial foreground engine or an additional/background engine. The Crashlytics event has no app logs or custom keys; the Play native stack identifies the context-creation stage, not the launching action.

### Expected results

Engine context creation should not abort the process inside the vendor profile library. A normal Vulkan initialization error could permit a renderer fallback, but this native abort occurs before the driver returns a `VkResult`.

### Actual results

One report / one impacted user on `SM-S901N`, Android 14, ARM64, in the bounded production query October 27 00:00 UTC through October 30 08:00 UTC, 2026 (end exclusive). The event was captured on October 30; Google Play buckets its event time to 03:00 UTC.

Scudo detects invalid chunk state during deallocation. The exact first corrupting operation, double-free versus another corruption mechanism, and driver version are unknown. The report does not include an abort-message string, so we are identifying the allocator error from the symbolized native stack.

### Code sample / application integration

No minimal reproducer is available yet. Relevant integration details, to avoid presenting this as a clean stock-Flutter reproduction:

- This is a **Shorebird-based Flutter 3.47.8 production release**, not an unmodified official Flutter binary.
- Native application bootstrap probes `GL_RENDERER` / `GL_VERSION` using a temporary EGL pbuffer before Flutter initialization. It restores the prior EGL binding and destroys the temporary resources. The app's driver gate targets affected Mali GLES drivers; Adreno normally retains Flutter's default Impeller selection. We have not verified whether this temporary EGL probe contributes to the crash.
- The application uses a cached audio-service Flutter engine and `firebase_messaging` 17.0.1, which can create a background engine. The particular engine's owner and any concurrent initialization at the incident are unknown.
- We have not reproduced this on an official Flutter SDK, Flutter 3.47.9, or current master, and have not verified an Impeller-disabled workaround on the affected physical device.

### Related reports and scope

- **#168665 (closed):** closest recorded Scudo variant; matching system/vendor PCs through Vulkan instance creation. It was closed as a duplicate of #166410. We are not assuming all failure variants in that thread had the same cause.
- **#176775 (open):** same `ContextVK::Setup` / `ApplyApplicationProfile` family. Its original failure is a destroyed-mutex FORTIFY abort, whereas this report is Scudo invalid chunk state during deallocation. A shared underlying cause is unproven.
- **#179921 (open):** also has `scudo::reportInvalidChunkState` during deallocation, but on a vivo / MediaTek `libsrv_um.so` path, not Qualcomm `libadreno_app_profiles.so`. Its stack does not establish our `ContextVK::Setup` / `ApplyApplicationProfile` call chain. Related allocator symptom, not an asserted duplicate.

Other Scudo mentions such as #194930 (possible `internal map failure` associated with retained Mali contexts) and #160941 (allocation/GPU memory exhaustion) appear different from this invalid-chunk deallocation signature; we have no evidence connecting this event to OOM.

The lifetime fix #166725 is already an ancestor of our deployed SDK revision, and its device/allocator keepalive is present. This alone does not prove a regression in that fix or rule out an application-integration contribution.

Could the engine team confirm whether this Scudo/profile-initialization variant is covered by the previous duplicate resolution, or should be tracked independently, and what additional driver/initialization diagnostics would help?

### Logs

The following are Google Play-provided symbolized frames 0–16, with application installation paths replaced by `<app>`. The large Flutter symbol offsets are retained as emitted by Play. The remaining shell/message-loop frames are omitted. The engine GNU BuildID was independently checked against the ARM64 `libflutter.so` embedded in the matching Shorebird SDK artifact and matches exactly.


title: flutter test hangs after a failed test compilation instead of exiting
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Our tests hung indefinitely on a 4-CPU, 8 GB RAM Ubuntu VM with the default 2GB size of /tmp. /tmp was nearly filled with 200 MB dill files from various runs, and a test run with `flutter test --no-pub --file-reporter json:test.log --concurrency=4` hung with no CPU activity for hours. 

This is easy to reproduce:

1. Create a Flutter package with a few widget tests, for example six copies of:
      ```dart
      import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
      import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
      
      void main() {
        testWidgets('shows a text', (WidgetTester tester) async {
          await tester.pumpWidget(const MaterialApp(home: Text('a')));
          expect(find.text('a'), findsOneWidget);
        });
      }
      ```
2. Run flutter test once and note the size of build/test_cache/build/*.dill. In this project it is 45 MB.
3. Create a small RAM disk, about 1.5× that size. It must fit one compiler output (output.dill) but not another dill file of similar size:
    macOS:
    ```sh
    device=$(hdiutil attach -nomount ram://$((75 * 2048)) | awk '{print $1}')
    diskutil erasevolume HFS+ FlutterTestTmp "$device"
    ```
    Linux:
    ```sh
    mkdir /tmp/small && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=75m,mode=1777 tmpfs /tmp/small
    ```
4. Delete the test cache and run the tests with TMPDIR on the RAM disk:
    ```sh
    rm -rf build
    TMPDIR=/Volumes/FlutterTestTmp flutter test --concurrency=4   # Linux: TMPDIR=/tmp/small
    ```

The attached repro.sh does steps 2–4 automatically, then stops flutter test after a timeout and removes the RAM disk.



### Expected results

flutter test exits with a non-zero exit code.


### Actual results

flutter test hangs indefinitely.

Claude Code suggested the following cause and fix:
```
## Cause in the code (test_compiler.dart, _onCompilationRequest)

The while (compilationQueue.isNotEmpty) loop has no try/catch/finally. An exception from recompile, the file copies, generateMainDartWithPluginRegistrant or createCompiler leaves the queue head in place and ends the loop. Later calls return at if (!isEmpty) return;.
A second problem in the same loop: if recompile returns null, the check outputPath == null || compilerOutput!.errorCount > 0 short-circuits into compilerOutput!.errorMessage, which throws a null-check error. That leads to the same hang.

## Suggested fix

Wrap each iteration in try/catch/finally:

On an exception, complete the request with a TestCompilerFailure that carries the error, and shut down the compiler.
Always call compilationQueue.removeAt(0) in finally.
Use compilerOutput?.errorMessage in the failure branch.
```

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

repro.sh:
```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Claude Code, but it seems to run fine.
#
# Reproduces `flutter test` hanging forever when TestCompiler fails to copy
# a compiled test file, here because TMPDIR runs out of space.
#
# 1. Runs the tests normally and measures the size of the compiled test dill.
# 2. Creates a RAM disk about 1.5 times that size: enough for the compiler
#    output (output.dill), but not for the copy TestCompiler makes of it next
#    to the test listener.
# 3. Runs the tests again with TMPDIR on the RAM disk. Expected: the tests
#    fail with a file system error. Actual: flutter test hangs.
#
# Works on macOS (hdiutil, no sudo) and Linux (tmpfs, needs sudo).
# Usage: ./repro.sh [timeout-seconds]
set -euo pipefail

timeout_seconds="${1:-300}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

flutter --version | head -n 1
flutter pub get >/dev/null

echo
echo "== Control run with the default TMPDIR"
rm -rf build
flutter test --concurrency=4
dill="$(ls build/test_cache/build/*.dill)"
dill_mb=$(( $(wc -c < "${dill}") / 1024 / 1024 ))
disk_mb=$(( dill_mb * 3 / 2 + 8 ))
echo "Compiled test dill: ${dill_mb} MB, RAM disk: ${disk_mb} MB"

tmp_dir=""
device=""
test_pid=""
cleanup() {
  if [[ -n "${test_pid}" ]] && kill -0 "${test_pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Stop flutter test and the frontend_server it started.
    kill -TERM -- "-${test_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" && -n "${device}" ]]; then
    hdiutil detach "${device}" -force >/dev/null || true
  elif [[ -n "${tmp_dir}" ]]; then
    sudo umount "${tmp_dir}" || true
    rmdir "${tmp_dir}" || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
  device="$(hdiutil attach -nomount "ram://$(( disk_mb * 2048 ))" | awk '{print $1}')"
  diskutil erasevolume HFS+ FlutterTestTmp "${device}" >/dev/null
  tmp_dir=/Volumes/FlutterTestTmp
else
  tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  sudo mount -t tmpfs -o "size=${disk_mb}m,mode=1777" tmpfs "${tmp_dir}"
fi

echo
echo "== Run with TMPDIR=${tmp_dir} (${disk_mb} MB), timeout ${timeout_seconds} s"
rm -rf build
# Job control puts flutter test in its own process group, so cleanup can
# stop all of its processes.
set -m
TMPDIR="${tmp_dir}" flutter test --concurrency=4 &
test_pid=$!
set +m

waited=0
while kill -0 "${test_pid}" 2>/dev/null && (( waited < timeout_seconds )); do
  sleep 1
  waited=$(( waited + 1 ))
done

echo
if kill -0 "${test_pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "== HANG: flutter test is still running after ${timeout_seconds} s"
  df -h "${tmp_dir}"
  ps -o pid,stat,time,command -p "$(pgrep -g "${test_pid}" | paste -sd, -)" |
    cut -c1-160
  exit 1
fi

set +e
wait "${test_pid}"
status=$?
set -e
echo "== flutter test exited with ${status} after ${waited} s (no hang)"
```

title: `flutter test --platform=chrome` per-suite load time regressed ~40% after `--no-js-strongly-connected-components`
body:
After [#193485](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/193485) ("Set --no-js-strongly-connected-components for DDC compiles by default") landed, `flutter test --platform=chrome` takes noticeably longer to load **each test suite**. DDC now emits one JS file per library, and each test suite gets its own iframe that loads the full set of scripts, so every suite pays the larger script count again.

In flutter/packages CI, the per-suite load time for `packages/material_ui` went from **~3.2 s to ~4.5–5 s** on the master channel at the roll that brought in #193485. The number of scripts each suite loads went from **1053 to 1537**. Stable doesn't include #193485 yet and stayed flat at ~2.2 s over the same period.

> **Note:** I'm not sure why `stable` was already ~1 s faster than master. That requires further investigation.

That PR's description says overall load time improves for large apps. For the web test runner the trade-off goes the other way: a package with N test files loads the app N times.

## Impact

- `packages/material_ui` has ~214 test files in `test/` and ~279 in `example/`.
  On master CI, loading suites accounts for roughly **35 of the ~43 minutes**
  of its web unit test step.
- Stable will pick up the same slowdown when #193485 reaches a stable release.

## Evidence

### Step change lines up with the roll that includes #193485

flutter/packages postsubmit, builder `Linux_web web_dart_unit_test_shard_N master`, package `packages/material_ui`. The "load time" column is the mean number of seconds between a `loading <file>` progress line and the next progress line, averaged over every suite in the package.

| Date (UTC) | packages commit | Flutter master pinned | Load time per suite | Scripts per suite | Build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-26 | `15e15cc9ed` | `55b8f88e855f` | 3.27 s | — | [8669642115610387905](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669642115610387905) |
| 2026-09-30 09:04 | `46c82808de` | `55b8f88e855f` | 3.22 s | **1053** | [8669246716962923297](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669246716962923297) |
| — | `913650f58d` | **Roll `55b8f88e855f` → `d649d2bfebfe`** (flutter/packages#13080), includes `b2977965ce` (#193485) | | | |
| 2026-09-30 21:06 | `6f110204ca` | `d649d2bfebfe` | 4.65 s | **1537** | [8669201311584671601](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669201311584671601) |
| 2026-10-01 | `d5ec6dbaf1` | | 4.29 s | — | [8669187090472438001](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669187090472438001) |
| 2026-10-14 | `975717a8bb` | | 5.19 s | — | [8667954581964520465](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8667954581964520465) |
| 2026-10-28 | `13d38e0d97` | | 4.76 s | 1564 | [8666728765165495921](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666728765165495921) |

The script counts come from DDC's own console output in the test logs:

```
[BROWSER CONSOLE] [info]: DDC is about to load 1053/1053 scripts with pool size = 100   # before
[BROWSER CONSOLE] [info]: DDC is about to load 1537/1537 scripts with pool size = 100   # after
```

From July to September, ~20 sampled master builds were steady at 2.8–3.5 s (occasionally 3.9 s), then jumped at this roll. Of the 27 framework commits in the roll, #193485 is the only one that changes DDC compilation or module output.

### Ruled out: Chrome version

- Master went from Chrome 125 to 145 on 2026-08-19 (flutter/packages#12486).
  The load time didn't change: 3.10 s on Aug 13, 2.76 s on Aug 20.
- Stable went from Chrome 125 to 137 on 2026-09-04 (flutter/packages#12747).
  The load time didn't change: ~2.2 s throughout.

## Reproduction (suggested)

# With a Flutter checkout at b2977965ce^ and then at b2977965ce:

Compare the time between consecutive `loading ...` lines, or the total wall time.

title: The raster thread uses freed memory when an external texture is unregistered while it is drawn
body:
### Steps to reproduce

**This was found by Claude while developing my macOS app, I'm confident it is a true bug.**

### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=macos repro`
2. Replace `lib/main.dart` and `macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift` with the two files below.
3. `flutter run -d macos`

The app shows four textures and keeps replacing each with a new one. It unregisters the old texture with `unregisterTexture:` while it is still on screen: the `Texture` widget shows the new id from the next frame on. This is what an app does when it moves a video into a new texture, or when a view showing a texture goes away.

### Expected results

Unregistering a texture that the last frame still shows is safe. The engine keeps what it needs until the raster thread is done with it.

### Actual results

The app crashes within 2 seconds, in 6 runs out of 6.
- Four runs stopped with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` and two with an `NSException` (`doesNotRecognizeSelector:`). All of them crashed on `io.flutter.raster`, in `+[FlutterDarwinExternalTextureImpellerImageWrapper wrapRGBATexture:aiksContext:]`, called from `EmbedderExternalTextureMetal::ResolveTexture`.
- The faulting addresses are those of freed memory: `0x10` and `0x20` when it was zeroed, and random ones once another allocation reused it. In our app, which hits the same crash, `MallocScribble=1` with `MallocZeroOnFree=0` gives `0x5555555555550002`.
- The setup: Flutter 3.47.5, macOS 27.2 on an M1 Pro, a debug build, Impeller on Metal.

What happens, in 3.47.5's source:
1. [`FlutterTextureRegistrar.mm` L48-L55](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.5/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterTextureRegistrar.mm#L48-L55): `unregisterTexture:` removes the `FlutterExternalTexture` from `_textures` on the caller's thread, the platform thread. That drops the only long-lived reference to it.
2. [`FlutterTextureRegistrar.mm` L57-L59](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.5/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterTextureRegistrar.mm#L57-L59): `getTextureWithID:` reads the same `NSMutableDictionary` on the raster thread, with no lock.
3. [`FlutterExternalTexture.mm` L134-L141](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.5/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterExternalTexture.mm#L134-L141): `populateTextureFromRGBAPixelBuffer:` stores an unretained `id<MTLTexture>` in the object's `std::vector`, releases the `CVMetalTexture`, and hands out `_textures.data()`, a pointer into the object.
4. [`embedder_external_texture_metal.mm` L62-L74](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.5/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/embedder/embedder_external_texture_metal.mm#L62-L74): `ResolveTexture` reads `texture->textures[0]` after the callback has returned, and only then wraps (retains) it.

So when `unregisterTexture:` runs while the raster thread is between steps 3 and 4, the `FlutterExternalTexture` is deallocated as soon as `populateTextureWithIdentifier:` returns:
- its vector's buffer is freed;
- the `FlutterTexture` it held is released, and with it the pixel buffer;
- `ResolveTexture` then messages a dangling `id<MTLTexture>`.

`FlutterMetalExternalTexture` has no `user_data` or destruction callback that could keep it alive. The comment in `embedder.h`, "These textures are retained by the engine for the period of the composition", isn't what happens here.

Possible fixes:
- Keep the `id<MTLTexture>` (or the `CVMetalTexture`) alive until the frame is drawn, for example by wrapping it while the `FlutterExternalTexture` is still held.
- Or remove the entry from `_textures` on the raster thread, after the engine's own unregistration, which already runs there.
- In both cases, guard `_textures` with a lock, since `registerTexture:` changes it on the platform thread too.

Workaround: call `unregisterTexture:` a while after the widget stopped showing the texture. We wait 500 ms.

Possibly related: #78056, from 2021. It had the same stack on the Skia path, from another cause, which flutter/engine#24995 fixed.



### Expected results

No crashes

### Actual results

Crashes.

### Code sample

### Code sample

<details open><summary>lib/main.dart</summary>

```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

const channel = MethodChannel('repro');

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Swapper()));

/// Shows four textures, and keeps replacing each with a new one. The old texture is unregistered
/// while it is still on screen: the view shows the new one from the next frame on.
class Swapper extends StatefulWidget {
  const Swapper({super.key});

  @override
  State<Swapper> createState() => _SwapperState();
}

class _SwapperState extends State<Swapper> {
  final List<int?> textureIds = List.filled(4, null);
  int swaps = 0;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    for (var i = 0; i < textureIds.length; i++) {
      swapForever(i);
    }
  }

  Future<void> swapForever(int i) async {
    while (mounted) {
      final old = textureIds[i];
      final id = await channel.invokeMethod<int>('register');
      if (old != null) await channel.invokeMethod('unregister', old);
      setState(() => textureIds[i] = id);
      if (++swaps % 1000 == 0) debugPrint('$swaps swaps');
      await Future.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 10));
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Center(
        child: Wrap(children: [
          for (final id in textureIds)
            SizedBox(width: 200, height: 200, child: id == null ? null : Texture(textureId: id)),
        ]),
      );
}
```

</details>

<details open><summary>macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift</summary>

```swift
import Cocoa
import CoreVideo
import FlutterMacOS

/// A texture that always shows the same BGRA pixel buffer
final class SolidTexture: NSObject, FlutterTexture {
  private let pixelBuffer: CVPixelBuffer

  override init() {
    var buffer: CVPixelBuffer?
    let attributes =
      [
        kCVPixelBufferMetalCompatibilityKey as String: true,
        kCVPixelBufferIOSurfacePropertiesKey as String: [String: Any](),
      ] as CFDictionary
    CVPixelBufferCreate(kCFAllocatorDefault, 256, 256, kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA, attributes, &buffer)
    pixelBuffer = buffer!
    CVPixelBufferLockBaseAddress(pixelBuffer, [])
    if let base = CVPixelBufferGetBaseAddress(pixelBuffer) {
      memset(base, 0x80, CVPixelBufferGetDataSize(pixelBuffer))
    }
    CVPixelBufferUnlockBaseAddress(pixelBuffer, [])
    super.init()
  }

  func copyPixelBuffer() -> Unmanaged<CVPixelBuffer>? {
    return Unmanaged.passRetained(pixelBuffer)
  }
}

class MainFlutterWindow: NSWindow {
  /// Each registered texture's frame notifications, as a video would send them
  private var frameTimers: [Int64: Timer] = [:]

  override func awakeFromNib() {
    let flutterViewController = FlutterViewController()
    let windowFrame = self.frame
    self.contentViewController = flutterViewController
    self.setFrame(windowFrame, display: true)

    RegisterGeneratedPlugins(registry: flutterViewController)

    let registrar = flutterViewController.registrar(forPlugin: "Repro")
    let textures = registrar.textures
    let channel = FlutterMethodChannel(name: "repro", binaryMessenger: registrar.messenger)
    channel.setMethodCallHandler { [weak self] call, result in
      guard let self else { return }
      switch call.method {
      case "register":
        let id = textures.register(SolidTexture())
        self.frameTimers[id] = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1.0 / 120, repeats: true) {
          _ in textures.textureFrameAvailable(id)
        }
        result(id)
      case "unregister":
        let id = (call.arguments as! NSNumber).int64Value
        self.frameTimers.removeValue(forKey: id)?.invalidate()
        textures.unregisterTexture(id)
        result(nil)
      default:
        result(FlutterMethodNotImplemented)
      }
    }

    super.awakeFromNib()
  }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the code sample below for web (`flutter run -d web-server`, debug or release).
2. Open it in Chrome on Android with **Desktop site** on. Chrome turns it on by default on large tablets such as the Pixel Tablet; on a phone, tick ⋮ > Desktop site.
3. Tap Email, type anything, and tap the keyboard's Next key (Gboard).

### Expected results

Focus moves to Password, as it does with Desktop site off.

### Actual results

Focus stays in Email. No keydown reaches the page. Event trace on a Pixel Tablet:

1. `blur` on the Email input, with `relatedTarget` = the hidden autofill `<input type="password" autocomplete="current-password">` in the engine's `<form>`.
2. `focus` back on the Email input.

Controls on the same devices:

- **Desktop site off:** Email gets `enterkeyhint="next"`, Chrome sends Enter (keyCode 13), and focus moves to Password.
- **Desktop site on, sample without the `AutofillGroup`:** Gboard labels the key "Go", Chrome sends Enter, and focus moves.

Cause, as far as we can tell from the sources:

1. **The engine sets no hint.** The desktop user agent (`X11; Linux x86_64`) has no "Android", so `ui_web.browser.operatingSystem` is Linux. `EngineInputAction.configureInputAction` then sets no `enterkeyhint`, and `inputmode` is left off too, so there is no email keyboard either.
2. **Chrome moves focus instead of sending Enter.** With no `enterkeyhint`, Chrome's `ImeAdapterImpl.performEditorAction` handles `IME_ACTION_NEXT` with `advanceFocusForIME`. It labels the key Next because the hidden autofill password input is the next focusable text control in the form. That input has no `tabIndex`; the active input and the submit input both have `-1`.
3. **The engine pulls focus back.** The related target is in the same view, so `DefaultTextEditingStrategy.handleBlur` moves focus back to the active input (the TODO citing #166857). `maybeSendAction` never sees a keydown, and the framework never receives `TextInputAction.next`.

Browser values in this mode, the same on two Pixel Tablets:
- `navigator.userAgent` is `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/156.0.0.0 Safari/537.36`
- `navigator.platform` is `Linux armv81`
- `navigator.maxTouchPoints` is `5`
- `navigator.userAgentData.platform` is `Linux` (`mobile: false`)

Possible fixes:

- **Detect Android in desktop mode** the way `browser_detection.dart` already detects iPadOS in desktop mode (a Mac platform with `maxTouchPoints > 2`), for example an ARM Linux `navigator.platform` with touch points. This would also restore `inputmode` and `TargetPlatform.android` on these tablets. Caveat: ARM Linux touch devices would read as Android.
- **Give the hidden autofill inputs `tabIndex = -1`,** as the active input and the submit input already have. Checked by setting it from page JavaScript: Chrome then labels the key "Go", sends Enter, and focus moves.
- **Set `enterkeyhint` whatever the detected OS.** Desktop keyboards ignore it; this was raised in the flutter/engine#35411 review.

Related: #180144 (a different bug in the same Android Desktop-site mode), #100708 (where `enterkeyhint` was added for mobile operating systems only).

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: LoginForm()));

class LoginForm extends StatelessWidget {

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const Scaffold(

        padding: EdgeInsets.all(32),
        child: AutofillGroup(
          child: Column(
            children: [
              TextField(
                autofillHints: [AutofillHints.email],
                keyboardType: TextInputType.emailAddress,
                textInputAction: TextInputAction.next,
                decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Email'),
              ),
              TextField(
                obscureText: true,
                autofillHints: [AutofillHints.password],
                textInputAction: TextInputAction.done,
```

body:
### Steps to reproduce

After upgrading to `shared_preferences_android` 2.5.x, restarting a secondary FlutterEngine causes subsequent SharedPreferences access to fail with:

```text
ArgumentError: Invalid argument(s): No instance with no name has been registered.

#0      _throwNoInstanceError
        (package:shared_preferences_android/src/messages.g.dart:180:3)
#1      SharedPreferencesApiForNativeInterop.getInstance
        (package:shared_preferences_android/src/messages.g.dart:240:9)
#2      new SharedPreferencesApi.createWithNativeInteropApi
        (package:shared_preferences_android/src/messages.g.dart:435:65)
#3      SharedPreferencesAndroid.api
        (package:shared_preferences_android/src/shared_preferences_android.dart:28:44)
```

My application uses `flutter_foreground_task`, which creates a secondary FlutterEngine for its foreground-service task. The error occurs when that service/engine is restarted.

The same application works without the exception when pinning:

```yaml
dependency_overrides:
  shared_preferences_android: 2.4.28
```

Removing the override and using `shared_preferences_android` 2.5.4 reproduces the problem.

This appears to be a regression introduced by the Pigeon JNI migration in `shared_preferences_android` 2.5.0 and may be related to registration/unregistration of the unnamed native-interoperability instance when multiple FlutterEngines attach and detach.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an Android Flutter application using `shared_preferences`.
2. Create a secondary FlutterEngine, for example through `flutter_foreground_task`.
3. Access SharedPreferences normally.
4. Stop/restart the secondary engine/service.
5. Access SharedPreferences again.

### Expected results

Detaching or restarting one FlutterEngine must not invalidate SharedPreferences registration used by another active/recreated FlutterEngine.

### Actual results

SharedPreferences throws:

```text
Invalid argument(s): No instance with no name has been registered.
```

### Code sample

### Regression

Works with:

```text
shared_preferences_android 2.4.28
```

Fails with:

```text
shared_preferences_android 2.5.4
```

The relevant change between these versions appears to be the migration to Pigeon JNI in 2.5.0.

title: [image_picker] iOS saves transparent images it can't write back, such as WebP, as JPEG
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On iOS, save a WebP with transparent pixels to Photos.
2. Pick it with `ImagePicker().pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery)`.
3. Inspect the returned file.

### Expected results

The file keeps its transparency, as on Android, where `ImageResizer` saves a bitmap with alpha as PNG.

### Actual results

The file is a `.jpg`, so its transparent pixels are gone.

`ImagePickerMetaDataUtil.getImageMIMEType` returns `.other` for anything but JPEG, PNG and GIF, and `.other` is encoded as JPEG. Nothing checks for an alpha channel.

Reproduced on `main` in `RunnerTests` on an iOS 26.2 simulator, by passing a transparent WebP through `PHPickerSaveImageToPathOperation` rather than by hand through Photos. The ICO and ICNS test images, which also have alpha, are affected in the same way.

### Code sample

```dart
final XFile? file = await ImagePicker().pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery);
print(file?.path); // Ends in .jpg for a transparent WebP.
```

### Flutter Doctor output

```
Flutter 3.47.7 • channel stable
image_picker_ios 0.8.13+14
```

body:
### Steps to reproduce

```dart
const a = ButtonThemeData();
const b = ButtonThemeData(layoutBehavior: ButtonBarLayoutBehavior.constrained);
print(a == b);
```

### Expected results

`false`, since the two themes have different `layoutBehavior` values.

### Actual results

`true`. `ButtonThemeData.==`, `hashCode` and `debugFillProperties` don't include `layoutBehavior`. Because `ButtonTheme.updateShouldNotify` compares `data`, changing only `layoutBehavior` also doesn't notify widgets that depend on the theme.

Seen in `packages/material_ui/lib/src/button_theme.dart` on main of flutter/packages (material_ui 1.9.0).

[web] Semantics on: mouse click on a button next to a focused TextField leaves EditableText focused but engine editing off (_isIntegerCoordinateNavigation + deferred safeBlur)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Flutter 3.47.0 stable (framework 4cf2416426, engine 5f77625673), web, `--wasm` (also seen with dart2js), semantics enabled (`SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`), Chrome desktop with a real mouse.

1. A `TextField` is focused and the user is typing.
2. Next to it is an `IconButton` that clears the field (for example a search ✕). It is visible only while the field has text.
3. Click the ✕ with the mouse.
4. Type again without clicking anything.

### Expected results

The field keeps focus and the new keys are inserted, as on every other platform and with semantics off.

### Actual results

Flutter still shows the field focused (focused underline, `FocusNode.hasFocus == true`, `EditableText` keeps the connection), but `document.activeElement` is `<flutter-view>`. The keys go nowhere. This happened in 10 of 10 runs in a Playwright trace with real Chrome pointer and keyboard input.

### Analysis

1. `EnginePlatformDispatcher._addNavigationFocusHandler` installs a capture-phase `click` listener. `_isLikelyAssistiveTechnologyActivation` → `_isIntegerCoordinateNavigation` treats a click whose `clientX`/`clientY` are whole numbers on a `role="button"` semantics node as an assistive-technology activation and calls `focusWithoutScroll()` on the button.
   Chrome reports whole-number `clientX`/`clientY` for ordinary mouse clicks at DPR 1, so every real mouse click on a button counts as an AT activation. A `mousedown` `preventDefault()` does not help, because the focus is moved by this `click` handler.
2. The focus move blurs the semantics `<input>`. `SemanticsTextEditingStrategy.disable()` then calls `viewManager.safeBlur(activeDomElement)`, which defers `_transferFocusToViewRoot` with `Future(() => ...)`.
3. The framework's next frame still reports the text field as focused, so editing is re-enabled on the input. Then the stale deferred `safeBlur` runs and moves the focus to the view root. Engine text editing is now off, but the framework still thinks the field is focused, and nothing reconnects it.

A related trigger with the same symptom: if a tooltip shows or hides while a semantics text field is focused (for example a different `IconButton` slides under the still pointer after the ✕ disappears), the route's semantics subtree is wrapped or unwrapped. That moves the focused `<input>` in the DOM, so it blurs, focus ends on `<body>`, and the keys are lost.

Pressing Backspace instead of clicking the ✕ never reproduces it (5 of 5 passed).

### Workaround in our app

A capture-phase `focusout` listener for `input/textarea[data-semantics-role="text-field"]`. After `Timer.run` plus one frame, if the framework's primary focus is still that `EditableText` but `document.activeElement` is not its input, it calls `unfocus()` and, on the next frame, `requestKeyboard()` (with an explicit `scheduleFrame()`).

### Suggestion

- Do not use whole-number click coordinates as an AT signal. Desktop Chrome mouse clicks at DPR 1 always have whole-number coordinates. `PointerEvent.pointerType`, `detail == 0`, or the absence of a preceding `pointerdown` are more reliable signals.
- Cancel or re-check the deferred `safeBlur` if the element is re-enabled or focused again before the timer runs.

Video playback fails on Huawei Mate 60 Pro (Kirin 9000S / HarmonyOS 4.2) — native_window_set_buffer_count EINVAL
body:
### Summary

在 Huawei Mate 60 Pro 上，用 `video_player` 播放 H.264 视频失败（黑屏）。日志显示海思解码器在 SurfaceProducer/AHB 表面上的 buffer 协商失败：`native_window_set_buffer_count failed: Invalid argument (22)`。

这是已知问题 #166481 / #163420 的延伸：现有修复只覆盖 `Android ≤ 10` 的华为，本机是 Android 12（API 31）+ 麒麟 9000S，不在覆盖范围内。

### Device info

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 型号 | HUAWEI Mate 60 Pro（`Build.MODEL=ALN-AL00`） |
| 芯片 | Kirin 9000S（`ro.board.platform=kirin9000s`） |
| 系统 | HarmonyOS 4.2.0 / Android 12（API 31） |
| 复现插件 | video_player_android 2.9.5（默认 textureView / SurfaceProducer） |

### Error log

```
E/ACodec: [OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc] setting nBufferCountActual to 12 failed: -1010
E/ACodec: [OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc] setting nBufferCountActual to 11 failed: -1010
E/ACodec: [OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc] setting nBufferCountActual to 10 failed: -1010
E/ACodec: [OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc] setting nBufferCountActual to 9 failed: -1010
I/ACodec: [OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc] retry success nBufferCountActual 6
E/BufferQueueProducer: [ImageReader-...] setMaxDequeuedBufferCount: ... exceeds ...
E/Surface: IGraphicBufferProducer::setBufferCount(6) returned Invalid argument
E/ACodec: native_window_set_buffer_count failed: Invalid argument (22)
E/ACodec: Failed to allocate buffers after transitioning to IDLE state (error 0xffffffea)
E/MediaCodec: Codec reported err 0xffffffea ... while in state 5/STARTING
```

### Root cause

海思 `OMX.hisi.video.decoder.avc` 输出 buffer 数上限很小，ACodec 协商（12→11→10→9）一路被拒、最终定 6；随后对 AHB 表面 `setBufferCount(6)` 被 ImageReader/AHB 的 BufferQueue 拒绝，返回 EINVAL，解码器启动失败。

### Workaround

`VideoViewType.platformView`（SurfaceView）可绕过。

### Expected

`hasAndroidHardwareBufferDefect()` 应把麒麟 9000S 也纳入，使 `createSurfaceProducer()` 对它回退到 `SurfaceTextureSurfaceProducer`。

body:
### Steps to reproduce We have noticed that the Windows apps use unnecessary CPU usage, which is being noticed by some of our customer which profile background app battery consumption. 1. Start up a blank flutter app on Windows. 2. Start a windows performance analyzer trace (In an admin powershell window run `wpr -start power -filemode`). 3. Without interacting the windows flutter app at all, stop the trace after a minute or two (In the same admin powershell window run `wpr -stop .etl`). 4. Open the trace and drill down into Computation -> CPU Usage (precise) -> Filter the process to the windows flutter app running from step 1. 5. Observe the CPU usage graph for the process spikes every 14-16ms. It seems like this timer is there to detect trackpad gestures, but it runs at all times, even when the trackpad isn't being used. Attached is a couple of screenshots windows performance analysis of the current master engine, which show constant CPU activity when the app is idle (at commit 418d48f74c32) vs a patched engine I made, with changes in flutter_window.cc/.h and direct_manipulation.cc/.h. The patch stops the kDirectManipulationTimer timer from polling every ~14 ms while idle, and instead starts/stops it on touchpad interaction BEGIN/END instead. For reference, the experimental patch for this behavior can be found [here](https://github.com/scott-macky-eb/flutter/commit/2ae43034a184fea69b773c84cb3d3e422214ae3f). title: [Linux][Wayland] Beta 3.50: FlViewRendererSubsurface shows a black window on GNOME 50.6 + NVIDIA 615 (default `flutter create` app); GTK frame clock stops after the first paint
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=linux subsurface_probe && cd subsurface_probe && flutter build linux --release`
2. Run `build/linux/x64/release/bundle/subsurface_probe` in a native GNOME Wayland session on an NVIDIA GPU.

### Expected results

The counter demo appears.

### Actual results

The window opens at the right size with the title bar, but the client area stays solid black for as long as the app runs (tested for minutes, moved/resized the window, forced redraws). No GL/EGL errors on stderr, only:

```
[IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/embedder/embedder_surface_gl_impeller.cc(127)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLESSDF).
```

The same binary with `GDK_BACKEND=x11` (which takes the `FlViewRendererOpenGL` path) renders the app.

### What I could observe from the outside

- Attaching gdb to the running app and reading the toplevel's `GdkFrameClock` counter shows it stuck (e.g. 30) and it does not advance after `gtk_widget_queue_draw(toplevel)` + 2 s, i.e. GTK never paints the parent surface again after the first frames. `io.flutter.ui` / `io.flutter.rast` CPU time also stops growing.
- Widget tree is as expected: `GtkApplicationWindow > FlView > GtkEventBox > FlViewRendererSubsurface` with a correct allocation and `scale=2`.
- In a larger app (BlueBubbles, same engine) built the same way, the first resize logs
  `WARNING **: Timed out waiting for subsurface frame of size 2160x1440 (have 2560x1534)` on every launch, and moving the window made Mutter log
  `meta_wayland_surface_role_notify_subsurface_state_changed: assertion 'klass->notify_subsurface_state_changed' failed` (twice). The default app did not trigger the Mutter assertion in my runs.
- The 3.47 stable engine (OpenGL renderer, EGLImage sibling path) renders fine on this machine apart from the separate stale-frame problem reported in a different issue.
