title: [Linux][Wayland] Stable 3.47 shared-framebuffer path: GTK keeps presenting a stale frame after the EGLImage decouples from the frame texture (NVIDIA 615, GNOME 50)
body:
### Summary

With the stable 3.47 Linux embedder on a native Wayland session with the NVIDIA proprietary driver, a long-running app's window stops updating after many hours of uptime: Flutter keeps rendering new frames, GTK keeps painting, but GTK paints the *old* frame forever. Input still works (the app reacts, just invisibly). A window resize revives it, because that is the only thing that recreates the compositor framebuffer and its EGLImage.

I debugged this in the live, stuck process with gdb (no symbols needed, all calls through the public GTK/GL/EGL API) and can show that the EGLImage that `fl_framebuffer.cc` creates from the compositor texture no longer refers to the same storage as that texture: writes on one side are invisible on the other, in both directions.

This is the `FlCompositorOpenGL` / `fl_framebuffer_create_sibling` path that master removed in #192150 in favour of `FlViewRendererSubsurface`, so master/beta are not affected by design. Filing because every 3.47 stable app on NVIDIA+Wayland can hit it, and because the trigger is not a one-off.

### Environment

- App: BlueBubbles 2.1.5 (Flathub), engine `cf636b1dfb818dd6a3ff16e390e93b1a036969c8` (flutter-3.47-candidate.0), Impeller, OpenGL renderer
- Fedora 44, kernel 7.2.13, GNOME Shell 50.4 / Mutter, native Wayland session (`GDK_BACKEND=wayland`), GTK 3.24.51 (Flatpak runtime org.gnome.Platform//51)
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, driver 615.78.08 (libEGL_nvidia inside the sandbox too); display 3840x2160 at 1.25 fractional scale, window at scale factor 2 (frame 2004x3360)
- Seen 3 times in 3 days, each after many hours of uptime (the last one ~20 h after launch). No suspend/resume, no display mode change, no NVRM Xid in the journal; GPU memory was not under pressure.

### What the stuck process showed

All numbers below are from one occurrence, read with `glReadPixels` through gdb while the window was stuck (scripts attached).

1. Raster side is alive and correct. Breaking on `glBlitFramebuffer` on `io.flutter.rast` shows `present_layers` blitting layer FBO 4 into the compositor framebuffer (FBO 2, texture 3, 2004x3360) at every presented frame. Reading column 200 of texture 3 after the blit shows the *new* UI state (the chat the user clicked).
2. GTK side keeps painting, but stale. `fl_view_renderer_draw` → `fl_compositor_opengl_render` → `fl_framebuffer_create_sibling` → `gdk_cairo_draw_from_gl` runs on every redraw. Reading the sibling texture (a fresh `glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES` of the same `FlEGLImage` handle, `0x294d0142bb1`) at the `gdk_cairo_draw_from_gl` entry returns the *old* frame, identical (same md5) on every paint, for over an hour.
3. Not a synchronization race: injecting `glFinish()` on the raster thread after the blit, and forcing extra paints, changes nothing. Not an FBO/name problem: FBO 2's `GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0` is still texture 3, `glIsTexture(3)` is true, size matches. Not a leak of sibling FBOs: after 20 h only 3 FBOs exist in GDK's context (so #194840 is a separate issue). The "already a sibling" rule holds: `eglCreateImageKHR` on texture 3 returns `EGL_BAD_ACCESS`, as the spec requires.
4. The image is decoupled in both directions. Clearing the GTK-side sibling to magenta (`glClear` through an FBO on the sibling, `glFinish`) and then reading texture 3 on the raster thread shows no magenta at all; the raster texture still holds the new frame. So the texture and the EGLImage's siblings are backed by different memory.
5. Recreating the texture + EGLImage (what a resize does via `fl_framebuffer_new`) fixes it immediately; a 1-pixel resize from the compositor side (`org.gnome.Shell.Extensions.Windows.Resize`) is the user-level workaround.

A standalone C program that mirrors this exact pattern (two non-shared EGL contexts, texture + EGLImage in A, per-paint sibling in B, unsynchronised full-surface blits at 60 Hz, pauses, extra GPU load, GL and GLES variants) ran 38 minutes / 165k frames on the same GPU without reproducing it, so the trigger is something rarer than the steady-state sharing; I could not identify it. I am happy to run more experiments on this machine.

### Why I think the embedder should still care

The spec (EGL_KHR_image_base) makes the application responsible for synchronising sibling access across contexts; the 3.47 path writes the texture on the raster thread while GDK may still be sampling the previous sibling, with only a `glFlush`. Whether or not that is what makes the NVIDIA driver re-home the texture's storage, the stable branch has no way to detect or recover from a decoupled image: the framebuffer is only recreated on a size change.

Options for the stable branch (I can send a PR for whichever you prefer):
- cheapest: recreate the EGLImage (new texture) when the window is unmapped/mapped or on a periodic basis (hacky);
- better: give the raster thread something to wait on before it overwrites the texture (an `EGLSync` taken after GTK's draw), so there is never a write-after-read across contexts;
- or document the Wayland subsurface renderer as the fix and cherry-pick it, if that is feasible for 3.47.x.

### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately only "run a Flutter 3.47 app on NVIDIA 615 + GNOME Wayland for many hours and interact occasionally". Three occurrences in 3 days on this machine.

### Attachments

gdb scripts used for the readbacks (`purge.gdb`, `wt.gdb`, `fresh.gdb`), the trimmed outputs, and the standalone repro attempt (`eglshare.c`): https://gist.github.com/NelsonScott/b44f42154d84c003e7ed7665aa992664

For what it is worth, the beta (3.50) subsurface renderer, which replaces this path, does not render at all on this GNOME 50.6 + NVIDIA setup (black window with the default `flutter create` app); reported separately.

### Expected results

The window shows the frame Flutter rendered.

### Actual results

The window shows a frame from hours ago until it is resized.

### Flutter doctor

(from the Flatpak build: `flutter --version` 3.47.8, engine cf636b1dfb818dd6a3ff16e390e93b1a036969c8, Dart 3.12.x)

title: [iOS] Dragging a selection handle after the text gets shorter puts the selection past the end of the text, causing RangeError in TextSelectionOverlay
[Impeller] A ShaderMask with an ImageShader stops later ColorFilter.mode layers in the frame from applying
[web] With semantics on, a click on a text field's `<input>` that has no pointer events before it also sends `SemanticsAction.tap` to a tappable ancestor
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Put the code sample below in a new project. It enables semantics and wraps the page in a `GestureDetector` whose `onTap` dismisses the keyboard (a common pattern).
2. `flutter build web` (release or `--debug`), serve `build/web` over HTTP and open it in Chrome.
3. Click an empty part of the page once, so the page has keyboard focus. The `<input>` is now in the DOM as `input[aria-label="Name"]`.
4. In DevTools, run the line below, then click back into the page area within 3 seconds (use the empty area below the field, not the field):
   ```js
   setTimeout(() => document.querySelector('input[aria-label="Name"]').click(), 3000);
   ```
   The timer is there because running it straight from the console leaves the page without focus.
5. When the timer has fired, type a character.

This is a `click` on the `<input>` with no `pointerdown`/`pointerup` just before it. A real mouse click does not trigger the bug (see below).

### Expected results

The text field takes focus and shows the typed character. The ancestor's `onTap` does not fire: activating the field should not also activate the widget around it. A mouse click on the field behaves this way. On Android and iOS, from the embedders' source (`AccessibilityBridge.performAction` for `ACTION_CLICK`, `SemanticsObject.accessibilityActivate`), an accessibility tap is sent only to the activated node, never to its ancestors.

### Actual results

- `outer GestureDetector.onTap` is printed when the click fires.
- The field does not get focus: no focus underline, the label does not float, the typed character is not shown, and `onChanged` is never called.

Tested on Flutter 3.47.5 stable and on master (3.50.0-0.3.pre, framework e467decf60, engine 091f11f0d9, 2026-11-02). The same steps were run in Playwright with Chromium 153, Chrome 156, Edge 156, WebKit 26.6 and Firefox 155. All five fail with `element.click()`, in both the release (dart2js) build and a `--debug` build. All five work with a real mouse click (`page.mouse.click()` at the field's centre).

Controls (all five browsers, 3.47.5 and master):

| Variant | `input.click()` | real mouse click |
|---|---|---|
| Sample as below | outer `onTap` fires, field not focused, text not shown | field focused, text shown |
| `GestureDetector(excludeFromSemantics: true, ...)` | field focused, text shown | field focused, text shown |
| No `GestureDetector`; `TextField(onTapOutside: (_) => FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.unfocus())` | field focused, text shown | field focused, text shown |
| Sample, plus an extra `click` listener on the `<input>` that calls `event.stopPropagation()` (emulating the fix below) | field focused, text shown | field focused, text shown |

Keyboard only (Tab to the field, then Space or Enter) does not trigger it, because the browser sends no `click` to a text input in that case.

**Cause (from the engine source; the same on master):**

- `SemanticTextField` is created with `SemanticRole.blank` and has no `Tappable` behaviour. Its `<input>` has a `click` listener that only calls `editableElement.focusWithoutScroll()` and does not stop propagation:
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e467decf605cbf89e3fe50045bc4b1f4b82e6c7f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/text_field.dart#L429-L434
- So the `click` bubbles to the ancestor `flt-semantics` element that has the `GestureDetector`'s `Tappable` listener (`flt-tappable`):
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e467decf605cbf89e3fe50045bc4b1f4b82e6c7f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/tappable.dart#L62-L67
- `ClickDebouncer.onClick` sees no recent `pointerup`, treats it as a standalone click, and sends `SemanticsAction.tap` for the **ancestor's** node:
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e467decf605cbf89e3fe50045bc4b1f4b82e6c7f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/pointer_binding.dart#L289-L301
- With a real mouse click, the `pointerup` comes less than 50 ms before the `click`, so the debouncer drops the bubbled click and the framework's gesture arena gives the tap to the `TextField`. That is why only clicks without pointer events are affected:
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e467decf605cbf89e3fe50045bc4b1f4b82e6c7f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/pointer_binding.dart#L443-L454

For nested tappables the engine already prevents this: `_sendSemanticsTapToFramework` calls `click.stopPropagation()` because a click on an inner tappable would otherwise also tap its ancestor, "creating a double tap/click, which is wrong" (#134842):
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e467decf605cbf89e3fe50045bc4b1f4b82e6c7f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/pointer_binding.dart#L320-L328
Text fields do not go through that path, so they miss the fix.

**Who sends such clicks:** `Tappable`'s own doc says the engine forwards a standalone `click` as `SemanticsAction.tap` because "when an assistive technology is enabled the browser may not send us pointer events". Scripted clicks (`element.click()`, `dispatchEvent`) always come without pointer events. In current Chromium, an assistive-technology "default action" sends `pointerdown`/`pointerup` before the `click`. I checked this with MSAA `accDoDefaultAction` on Chrome 156 and Edge 156 on Windows: those do **not** trigger the bug. Reading WebKit's source, before https://commits.webkit.org/322978@main (2026-10-07), WebKit's accessibility press (for example VoiceOver's VO-Space on macOS) sent `mousedown`/`mouseup`/`click` with no pointer events. That is the event shape that triggers this bug. I have not tested it with VoiceOver.

**Suggested fix:** in `SemanticTextField`'s `click` listener, call `event.stopPropagation()` after `focusWithoutScroll()`, as `ClickDebouncer._sendSemanticsTapToFramework` does for tappable nodes, so activating a text field never also activates an ancestor. A listener on the `<input>` that does this fixed the repro in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox (last row of the table).

**Workarounds** (both tested above): `excludeFromSemantics: true` on the dismiss-keyboard `GestureDetector`, or dismiss with `TextField.onTapOutside` (`TapRegion`) instead of an ancestor `GestureDetector`.

Related, but not the same: #134842 (nested tappables, fixed with `stopPropagation`), #195291 (with semantics on, a click inside a `TextFieldTapRegion` stops typing; a different mechanism, browser focus moving to `flutter-view`).

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics();
  runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Home()));
}

class Home extends StatelessWidget {
  const Home({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return GestureDetector(
      // Common pattern: tap outside any field to dismiss the keyboard.
      onTap: () {
        debugPrint('outer GestureDetector.onTap');
        FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.unfocus();
      },
      child: Scaffold(
        body: Padding(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(24),
          child: TextField(
            decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Name'),
            onChanged: (String value) => debugPrint('onChanged: $value'),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

I can provide before/after screenshots for each browser: after `input.click()` and typing, the field is unfocused and empty; after a mouse click and typing, it is focused and shows the character.

</details>

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

After `input.click()`, then typing `x` (every browser above, 3.47.5 and master):

```console
outer GestureDetector.onTap
```

After a real mouse click on the field, then typing `x`:

```console
onChanged: x
```

</details>

title: [Impeller] Android: SIGSEGV on raster thread at startup with the OpenGL ES backend on Adreno 320 (no Vulkan, armeabi-v7a, Android 14)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create bug` with Flutter 3.47.9 stable. No changes to `lib/main.dart`.
2. `flutter build apk --release --target-platform android-arm`
3. Install on a Nexus 7 (2013) Wi-Fi: Adreno 320, OpenGL ES 3.0, no Vulkan driver, armeabi-v7a only, Android 14 (LineageOS 21).
4. Launch the app.

### Expected results

The counter app starts and stays open.

### Actual results

The app closes about 0.5 s after launch, every time. Impeller tries Vulkan, falls back to the OpenGL ES backend, then the raster thread crashes with SIGSEGV (fault addr 0x4):

```
I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).
F libc    : Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0x4 in tid 6706 (1.raster), pid 6681 (com.example.bug)
I Zygote  : Process 6681 exited due to signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
```

Same result on Flutter 3.47.1 (engine 5d53178869) and 3.47.9 (engine 89c39edfdf).

With `io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller=false` in the manifest, apps built with Flutter 3.47.x run normally on this device (tested with Plezy 2.25.0). The engine logs that this opt-out is deprecated, so once it is removed this device class has no working renderer.

Two release apps also crash the same way on this tablet: Plezy 2.25.0 (Flutter 3.47.1) and Obtainium 1.7.3. Plezy issue: https://github.com/edde746/plezy/issues/2948

Not a duplicate, as far as I can tell:
- #192365 (GLES use-after-free via `Picture.toImage` snapshots, closed 17 Oct): the counter app takes no snapshots, and it still crashes on 3.47.9.
- #195627 (`Image.toByteData()` with no surface): regression on `main` only; this app does not call it.
- #190640 (SIGABRT in ImageDecoderImpeller, Mali, Android 10): different signal, thread and GPU.
- #175562 (segfaults on older devices): Vulkan path, 64-bit. Possibly related.

No native backtrace: `crash_dump32` logs `failed to fetch registers for thread N: I/O error` for every thread (old 3.4 kernel), and no tombstone is stored in dropbox. I can collect an `adb bugreport`, or test a debug/profile build or a patch, if that helps.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

Unmodified counter template from `flutter create bug` (Flutter 3.47.9). `lib/main.dart` is byte-identical to the generated file.

Build-config changes, made only so it builds on a small Linux machine (they do not touch rendering):
- `android/gradle.properties`: `org.gradle.jvmargs` reduced from `-Xmx8G` to `-Xmx1536m`; daemon off.
- `android/app/build.gradle.kts`: `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` removed and `packaging { jniLibs { keepDebugSymbols += setOf("**/*.so") } }` added (no NDK installed for symbol stripping).

Full diff attached (`flutter-repro-build-diff-3.47.9.txt`).

</details>


### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

N/A. The splash shows, then the app closes.

</details>


### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

Device: Google/ASUS Nexus 7 (2013) Wi-Fi "flo", Snapdragon S4 Pro APQ8064, 2 GB RAM, armeabi-v7a only.
GPU: `GLES: Qualcomm, Adreno (TM) 320, OpenGL ES 3.0 V@145.0 AU@  (GIT@Id2569cc314)`, EGL `QUALCOMM Build: 02/11/16, 38a9cf9`.
No Vulkan: `vndksupport: Could not load vulkan.msm8960.so from default namespace: dlopen failed: library "vulkan.msm8960.so" not found.`

title: IconButton.filled uses the default IconTheme color during animated ThemeData changes
First hot reload after `flutter attach` fails for an app built with `flutter build ios --debug`
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms ios --org com.example app && cd app`
2. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below.
3. Build a debug app for the simulator: `flutter build ios --simulator --debug`
4. Install it on a booted simulator: `xcrun simctl install <udid> build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app`
5. Start `flutter attach -d <udid>`, then launch the app: `xcrun simctl launch <udid> com.example.app`
6. Change `'Hello'` to `'Hello again'` in `lib/main.dart` and press `r`.

### Expected results

The text changes to "Hello again", as with `flutter run`.

### Actual results

The app shows a red error screen with `Lookup failed: _location`. After one hot restart (`R`), hot reloads work.

`flutter build ios` has no `--track-widget-creation` option and writes `TRACK_WIDGET_CREATION=false` to `ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig`, while `flutter attach` defaults to `--track-widget-creation`. `flutter build apk` has the option and defaults it to on.

Attaching with `flutter attach -d <udid> --no-track-widget-creation` works around it. I'd expect `flutter build ios --debug` to track widget creation by default and accept `--[no-]track-widget-creation` like `flutter build apk`.

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/109602 looks like the same mismatch for add-to-app modules built from Xcode, but I haven't confirmed that.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MyApp());

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const Center(
      child: Text('Hello', textDirection: TextDirection.ltr),
    );
  }
}
```

title: `dart` run from a git hook in a linked worktree deletes bin/cache/flutter.version.json
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run this script from an empty directory, with Flutter on the `PATH`:

   ```bash
   SDK="$(flutter --version --machine | jq -r .flutterRoot)"
   git init -q demo && cd demo
   printf 'name: demo\nenvironment:\n  sdk: ^3.8.0\ndependencies:\n  flutter:\n    sdk: flutter\n' > pubspec.yaml
   git add pubspec.yaml && git commit -q -m init
   git worktree add -q ../demo-wt && cd ../demo-wt
   mkdir hooks && printf '#!/bin/sh\ndart --version\n' > hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x hooks/pre-commit
   ls "$SDK/bin/cache/flutter.version.json"
   git -c core.hooksPath=hooks commit -q --allow-empty -m trigger
   ls "$SDK/bin/cache/flutter.version.json"
   dart pub get
   ```

2. Run `flutter --version` to restore the file.

### Expected results

The hook runs `dart --version`, and the SDK is unchanged. `dart pub get` resolves the package.

### Actual results

The hook deletes `bin/cache/flutter.version.json` from the SDK. Every `dart pub get` and `dart run` that must resolve a Flutter package then fails. The failures continue until a `flutter` command writes the file again.

In a linked worktree, git sets `GIT_DIR` for hooks. `bin/internal/shared.sh` then runs `git -C "$FLUTTER_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD`, which returns the HEAD of the user's repository. The result does not match `bin/cache/flutter_tools.stamp`, so `upgrade_flutter` deletes `flutter.version.json` and `version`. When the wrapper is invoked as `dart`, it returns before it rebuilds the tool or writes the stamp. Nothing writes the file again.

With git 2.56.0, a commit in a repository's main checkout does not trigger this, because git does not set `GIT_DIR` there. #187150 reports that a plain repository sets it with git 2.39.5. Any other caller that exports `GIT_DIR` takes the same path.

#180421 and #187150 reported the same environment leak in the tool. #186595 fixed it there, and 3.47.9 includes that fix: `Git._filterEnvironment` removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and related variables. The shell wrapper still calls git with the inherited environment. I reproduced this on 3.47.9 and 3.44.8, and `master` has the same code. `shared.bat` has the same `rev-parse` and delete steps. `bin/internal/update_engine_version.sh` already unsets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` for its own git calls.

A possible fix is to apply the variable list from #186595 to the SDK's own git calls in `shared.sh` and `shared.bat`. The environment of the user's command must not change. A `dart` program run from a hook can depend on `GIT_DIR`.

### Code sample

The script in "Steps to reproduce" is the complete sample.

### Screenshots or Video

_No response_

### Logs

### Steps to reproduce

### Run a minimal project on iOS with two dependencies:
1. flutter_background_service (tested with ^5.1.0)
2. video_player (tested with 2.14.1)
and "background fetch" active.

### Using `flutter_background_service` schedule
```
    FlutterBackgroundService().configure(
      iosConfiguration: IosConfiguration(
        onForeground: null,
        onBackground: backgroundTaskIOS,
        autoStart: true,
      ),
      // not actually used, never run on Android!
      androidConfiguration: AndroidConfiguration(
        onStart: (_) {},
        isForegroundMode: false,
        autoStart: false,
        autoStartOnBoot: false,
      ),
    );
```

`backgroundTaskiOS` can just be an empty function:
```
@pragma('vm:entry-point')
FutureOr<bool> backgroundTaskiOS(ServiceInstance _) async {
  // nothing
}
```

When this job runs, the iOS app crashes due to the VideoPlayer plugin assuming to be run on the MainActor - while the FlutterEngine is actually disposed in a different Thread in the background isolate.

title: Impeller gradients can fail with sizes > 256px
body:
### Steps to reproduce Impeller shaders use mediump which some drivers (e.g. radeonsi) compute using fp16. This causes gradients of length > 256 px to incorrectly render. This did not occur using skia. ### Expected results When using a gradient of any length the colours smoothly change. ### Actual results Long gradients are shown with just the start and end colour an a hard boundary. ### Code sample
Code sample ```dart import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart'; void main() { const gradient = LinearGradient(colors: [Color(0xFFFF0000), Color(0xFF0000FF)]); runApp( const Column( children: [ // Works: the gradient position is at most 200 * 200, within fp16 (max 65504). SizedBox(width: 200, height: 100, child: DecoratedBox(decoration: BoxDecoration(gradient: gradient))), // Fails: 600 * 600 overflows fp16, so there is a hard edge at ~109 px. SizedBox(width: 600, height: 100, child: DecoratedBox(decoration: BoxDecoration(gradient: gradient))), ], ), ); } ```

title: [a11y] have a way to test that link nodes have an accessible name
body:
### Use case

WCAG SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (level A)
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html

A link needs an accessible name, but currently a semantics node flagged `isLink` with a non-empty `linkUrl` and no label passes every existing check:

```dart
Semantics(
  container: true,
  link: true,
  linkUrl: Uri.parse('https://flutter.dev'),
  child: const Icon(Icons.open_in_new),
)
```

- `LabeledTapTargetEvaluation` and the public `labeledTapTargetGuideline` skip any node that doesn't have a tap or long-press action, and a link node doesn't need either.
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/_accessibility_evaluations.dart#L264-L268
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter_test/lib/src/accessibility.dart#L259-L263
- `UnlabeledLeafNodeEvaluation` only checks nodes that `_isImportantForAccessibility` accepts, and that predicate has no `isLink` test. So a link node with no actions and no content gets skipped as well.
  https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/_accessibility_evaluations.dart#L792-L819

On web this node becomes an `<a href>`, so the browser puts it in the Tab order and a screen reader announces it as a link with no name.

Links that the framework builds with a tap action are already covered by the tap-target check. The gap is `Semantics(link: true, linkUrl: ...)` written by hand, with the name missing or left on unmerged children.

### Proposal

My proposal is to extend the accessible-name check on both surfaces:

- `LabeledTapTargetEvaluation` in `_accessibility_evaluations.dart`
- `LabeledTapTargetGuideline` in `flutter_test`

A node would also qualify when it is flagged `isLink` and has a non-empty `linkUrl`. Such a node with an empty label and tooltip reports a violation, including when its name only comes from unmerged descendants, which is how the check already treats tappable nodes today.

The `linkUrl` gate mirrors existing tools: axe-core's `link-name` rule selects `a[href]`, and W3C ACT rule c487ae applies to elements with the link role, which an `<a>` only has with an `href`. On Flutter web a link node without a `linkUrl` renders as an `<a>` without `href`, which isn't focusable (see #194551).

https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/link-name
https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core/blob/v4.10.0/lib/rules/link-name.json (the `a[href]` selector)
https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/act/rules/c487ae/

The existing users of the check should stay green: flutter_test's own accessibility tests, the flutter_gallery accessibility test, and over in flutter/packages, material_ui's `search_anchor_test.dart` and the a11y_assessments app (`packages/material_ui/test_apps/a11y_assessments`).

### Out of scope

- SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose, since whether the text describes the destination needs human judgment.
- Whitespace-only names, since trimming would change the current behavior for tappable nodes.
- The existing false positive on `SelectableText.rich` with a tappable span (a long-press node not flagged `isTextField`).

title: [Windows] Stable 3.47.8 still crashes in dart::ProfilerNativeStackWalker::walk — fix (sdk@0a7701) is on main but not in Dart 3.13 branch
body:
### Summary

Stable **3.47.8** (Dart **3.13.7**, engine `cf636b1dfb`) still crashes in `dart::ProfilerNativeStackWalker::walk` on Windows debug/profile runs. The same bug was reported and closed as fixed in #191069 — and it *is* fixed on `main` (dart-lang/sdk@0a7701121ede, *"[vm, profiler] Refine the stack boundary using the top SP"*), but that commit is **not** in the Dart 3.13 branch that ships with stable. This report is a **backport/cherry-pick request for the stable branch**, not a new root-cause investigation.

### Evidence that the fix is missing from stable

`GET /repos/dart-lang/sdk/compare/0a7701121ede...3.13.7` → `status: diverged`, `behind_by: 837`, i.e. the 3.13.7 tag does **not** contain `0a7701121ede`. Flutter 3.47.8 ships Dart 3.13.7 (`flutter doctor -v` below), which matches the crash we still reproduce.

### Root cause (confirmed independently by symbolication)

Crash signature is stable across runs: `0xC0000005` (read) at `flutter_windows.dll+0x92A350`, which the engine PDB resolves to:

```
dart::ProfilerNativeStackWalker::CallerFP   [inlined in walk+0x40]
dart::ProfilerNativeStackWalker::walk+0x40
dart::Profiler::SampleThread+0x151
dart::ProfilerDartStackWalker::WalkFromTopFrame   [inline]
dart::ThreadInterrupterWin::Interrupt+0xbc
dart::ThreadInterrupter::InterruptThread+0x3b
dart::ThreadInterrupter::ThreadMain+0x21e
dart::ThreadEntry+0x80
thread_start<...> → kernel32!BaseThreadInitThunk → ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart
```

The corresponding instruction is `mov rdi, qword ptr [rcx]`. `walk` *does* validate the frame pointer (non-null, 8-byte aligned, `fp+8` inside `[rsi+0x48, rsi+0x30)`), but the boundary itself is wrong. Two dumps from **independent processes**:

| | dump A | dump B |
|---|---|---|
| `fp` (`[rsi+0x40]`) | `0x0000000000100140` | `0x00000000001000c0` |
| lower bound `[rsi+0x48]` | `0x0000000000060000` | `0x0000000000060000` |
| upper bound `[rsi+0x30]` | `0x0000000000160000` | `0x0000000000160000` |
| `rsi` | `0x0000000051b6f850` | `0x0000000051b6f850` |
| `rip` | `flutter_windows+0x92A350` | `flutter_windows+0x92A350` |

The sampled thread's stack lives around `0x51b6xxxx`, yet the walker validates against `[0x60000, 0x160000)` — not a stack range at all. Because `fp` happens to be 8-byte aligned and inside that range, it passes every check and is dereferenced. The values are identical across processes, so this is a **deterministic wrong boundary**, which is exactly what `0a7701121ede` ("refine the stack boundary using the top SP") corrects.

### Reproduction on stable 3.47.8

| run | Dart sampling profiler | interaction | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flutter run -d windows` (debug) | on | synthetic pointer events | **crash**, fixed offset `+0x92A350` |
| debug exe launched directly + `FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCH_1=enable-dart-profiling=true` | on | same | **crash 4/4** |
| debug exe launched directly, switches unset | off | same | alive 4/4 |
| `flutter run -d windows --profile` | off (AOT) | same, 200 s | alive |

No `flutter` tool needed for the switch-only path:

```powershell
$env:FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCHES = "1"
$env:FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCH_1 = "enable-dart-profiling=true"
# launch any debug-built Windows exe directly, then interact with the UI
```

Note on how easily it triggers: the walker is only reached when the sampled thread is inside **native** code. A `flutter create` counter app hits it while clicking (as in #191069), but apps that keep threads inside FFI (llama.cpp / ONNX Runtime / sqlite) crash **within a couple of seconds** of any UI activity, which made bisecting deterministic. That may be why the original report looked "random".

### Logs / dumps

WER is disabled on this machine (`WerSvc` stopped/disabled, no Event ID 1000 entries, no WER report archive), so both dumps were captured with a small in-process handler in `windows/runner` (`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` + `MiniDumpWriteDump`). Symbolication:

```bash
export _NT_SYMBOL_PATH=""   # otherwise the engine's PDB URI hangs on the symbol server
cdb -z <dump> -y "D:\flutter\flutter\bin\cache\artifacts\engine\windows-x64" -c ".ecxr; kv; q"
```

Happy to attach the `.dmp` files (or the minimal harness) if useful.

### Ask

Please cherry-pick `dart-lang/sdk@0a7701121ede` into the Dart 3.13 stable branch (and roll it into the next stable hotfix), or tell us which stable release contains it. Until then, `flutter run -d windows` in debug mode is unusable on Windows for FFI-heavy apps, and `--profile` is only a workaround (no hot reload).

title: [CarouselView] Crash (RangeError / ArgumentError) when children or itemCount is empty with infinite: true or CarouselController.animateToItem
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `CarouselView` or `CarouselView.weighted` with `infinite: true` and an empty list of children: `children: const <Widget>[]`.
2. Run the application. Notice it immediately throws an unhandled `RangeError (length): Invalid value: Valid value range is empty: 0` during layout when constructing item 0.
3. Alternatively, create a `CarouselView.builder` with `infinite: true` and `itemCount: 0`. Notice the builder is invoked with indices 0, 1, 2, 3... despite `itemCount == 0`.
4. Alternatively, create a `CarouselView` with a `CarouselController` and an empty list of children (or `itemCount: 0`), and call `controller.animateToItem(0)`. Notice it throws an unhandled `ArgumentError: 'lowerLimit' (0) cannot be greater than 'upperLimit' (-1)`.

### Expected results

1. When `infinite: true` and `children.isEmpty` (or `itemCount == 0`), `CarouselView` / `CarouselView.weighted` / `CarouselView.builder` should render an empty scrollable viewport without throwing exceptions (matching the behavior when `infinite: false`).
2. `CarouselView.builder` should not invoke `itemBuilder` when `itemCount == 0`.
3. `CarouselController.animateToItem` should safely early-return or no-op when there are no items to animate to, rather than throwing an `ArgumentError` from `index.clamp(0, itemCount - 1)`.

### Actual results

1. For `CarouselView` and `CarouselView.weighted` with `infinite: true` and `children: const <Widget>[]`:
   ```
   ══╡ EXCEPTION CAUGHT BY WIDGETS LIBRARY ╞═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   The following RangeError was thrown building:
   RangeError (length): Invalid value: Valid value range is empty: 0

   When the exception was thrown, this was the stack:
   #0      _Array.[] (dart:core-patch/array.dart)
   #1      _CarouselViewState._buildCarouselItem (package:flutter/src/material/carousel.dart:635:38)
   #2      _CarouselViewState._buildSliverCarousel.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter/src/material/carousel.dart:686:63)
   #3      SliverChildBuilderDelegate.build (package:flutter/src/widgets/scroll_delegate.dart:553:22)
   #4      SliverMultiBoxAdaptorElement._build (package:flutter/src/widgets/sliver.dart:1061:28)
   ```

2. For `CarouselView.builder` with `infinite: true` and `itemCount: 0`:
   `itemBuilder` is called with indices 0, 1, 2, 3...

3. For `CarouselController.animateToItem(0)` on an empty `CarouselView`:
   ```
   ArgumentError: 'lowerLimit' (0) cannot be greater than 'upperLimit' (-1)
   package:flutter/src/material/carousel.dart:1972:25: CarouselController.animateToItem
   ```

### Root Cause

In `packages/flutter/lib/src/material/carousel.dart`:

1. In `_CarouselViewState._buildSliverCarousel`:
   ```dart
   final int? childCount = widget.infinite
       ? null
       : widget.itemBuilder != null
       ? widget.itemCount
       : widget.children.length;
   ```
   When `widget.infinite` is true, `childCount` is unconditionally set to `null` even if `children.isEmpty` or `itemCount == 0`. As a result, the sliver delegate builds child index 0:
   ```dart
   Widget contents = widget.children[index];
   ```
   which throws `RangeError (length)` because `widget.children` is empty.
   Additionally, in builder mode, `childCount: null` causes `itemBuilder` to be invoked indefinitely even though `itemCount == 0`.

2. In `CarouselController.animateToItem` (and `_getTargetOffset`):
   ```dart
   if (_carouselState!.widget.itemBuilder != null) {
     final int? itemCount = _carouselState!.widget.itemCount;
     index = itemCount != null ? index.clamp(0, itemCount - 1) : 0;
   } else {
     index = index.clamp(0, _carouselState!.widget.children.length - 1);
   }
   ```
   When `itemCount == 0` or `children.length == 0`, `itemCount - 1` evaluates to `-1`, leading to `index.clamp(0, -1)`, which throws `ArgumentError: 'lowerLimit' (0) cannot be greater than 'upperLimit' (-1)`.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MaterialApp(home: CarouselEmptyRepro()));
}

class CarouselEmptyRepro extends StatelessWidget {
  const CarouselEmptyRepro({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const Scaffold(
      body: Center(
        child: SizedBox(
          height: 200,
          child: CarouselView(
            itemExtent: 200.0,
            infinite: true,
            children: <Widget>[], // Throws RangeError (length): Invalid value: Valid value range is empty: 0
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

N/A

```

The following RangeError was thrown building:
```

title: Keep `flutter_driver` available for desktop apps and AI agents, or provide a supported replacement
body:
Coming from:

- https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/issues/651

_Some of this issue was drafted with an AI from the previous issue, but I've reviewed it fully._

---

## Summary

`flutter_driver` is being replaced by `integration_test`, but `flutter_driver` is available through MCP and currently cannot drive a running app the way agents need. Specifically, it cannot perform actions like right-clicking a widget, which is needed for desktop apps.

## Context

I'm using Flutter with a desktop app and an LLM agent (via the Dart MCP server) that drives the running app to check its own work, for example by taking screenshots, tapping widgets, and iterating on UI fixes.

Currently, `flutter_driver` makes this possible. The Dart MCP server exposes it through the `flutter_driver_command` tool. I wrote a skill to explain its subcommands, and it works relatively well.

However, I've seen that `flutter_driver` is being replaced by `integration_test` (and Gemini mentioned that to me). When my agent needed to right-click a widget in a desktop app, it couldn't, because `flutter_driver` doesn't support that interaction, only `integration_test` would.

At the original issue, @jakemac53 said (https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/issues/651#issuecomment-6610664283):

> I do agree, having this available for agents is useful, and integration_test is not a replacement for it.

## Questions

1. I want to confirm if there is any intention to keep `flutter_driver` supported, or to deprecate it
2. If it is being deprecated, what is the supported replacement for driving a running app programmatically, including desktop-specific interactions such as secondary (right) clicks or other interactions?
3. Would the team consider making this capability available for LLM agents to drive apps and verify their own changes?

## Why it matters

LLM agents are increasingly used to build and check Flutter apps. Being able to interact with a running app (tap, scroll, right-click, screenshot) lets agents verify their work without a human in the loop, which saves significant back-and-forth.

[iOS] Expose UITraitCollection.verticalBarEdge to the framework
body:
### Use case

Starting with iOS 27.1, on devices like iPhone Duo, the system can move the bars an app normally shows at the top or bottom into a vertical bar along one side of the screen. UIKit reports the side through `UITraitCollection.verticalBarEdge` (leading, trailing or none). Because it is a trait it changes at runtime, for example when the device folds or unfolds, when the app moves between the cover display and the inner display, or when the app opts in or out.

Flutter apps can't read this today. The space shows up as a safe area inset in `MediaQuery.padding`, but nothing tells the app why that edge is inset, so it can't tell the bar apart from a notch or cutout and can't put its own navigation there the way native apps do. Guessing the side from width, orientation or padding breaks in right-to-left locales and on the cover display. The workaround is a platform channel in every app that observes the trait per scene and converts the logical edge to a physical side.

### Proposal

Expose the bar edge next to the padding:

- Add `MediaQueryData.verticalBarEdge`, with its own aspect (`MediaQuery.verticalBarEdgeOf(context)`), typed as an enum like `VerticalBarEdge { none, left, right }` resolved to a physical side, since `padding` is physical as well. Keeping start/end and documenting that it follows `Directionality` would also work.
- Deliver it through `ViewportMetrics` / `FlutterView` so it updates in the same frame as the inset it explains.
- Report `none` on other platforms and on iOS versions before 27.1.

With that in place, Material and Cupertino could later dock `NavigationBar` or `CupertinoTabBar` on that edge (see #193878), but the value itself is useful on its own.

Related: #192515 and #193025 (display features from the hinge and reserved regions), #193054 (hinge events), #193878 (side docked navigation).

title: [Windowing] integration_test cannot test secondary windows: stand-in views reach the real text input plugin; a native owner segfaults on TestPlatformDispatcher.engineId == 1
body:
### Summary

At master 934720261be (`flutter config --enable-windowing`), an `integration_test` that opens a `WindowController` and types into a `TextField` in that window fails on Windows. You can also not switch the integration binding to real native windows.

1. **Default owner → errors on Windows.** `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.createWindowingOwner` installs `_TestWindowingOwner` when `registerTestWindowingOwner` is true. `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding` inherits that, so a `WindowController` there is a test view on `TestPlatformDispatcher` that the engine never sees. But the integration binding does **not** register `TestTextInput` (`registerTestTextInput => false`), so text input from a field in that window goes to the real platform with `viewId` 1. The Windows `TextInputPlugin` looks the view up on `setEditableSizeAndTransform`, `setMarkedTextRect` and `clearClient`, and fails each one:

   ```
   PlatformException(Internal Consistency Error, Text input is not available because view with view_id=1 cannot be found, null, null)
   #2 _PlatformTextInputControl.setEditableSizeAndTransform.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter/src/services/text_input.dart:2748:11)
   ```

   This happens three times per text session, while `platformDispatcher.views` reports `[0, 1]`. Linux passes because its plugin does not check the view.

2. **Native owner → segfault.** Setting `binding.windowingOwner = createDefaultWindowingOwner()` after `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` (the binding cannot be subclassed, since the integration entry point creates it before `main`) crashes the app on Linux on the first `WindowController(...)`. `TestPlatformDispatcher.engineId` is hard-coded to `1` (`packages/flutter_test/lib/src/window.dart:199`, from #173715). On Linux `_FlEngine(engineId)` is `Pointer.fromAddress(1)`:

   ```
   #0 g_type_check_instance_is_fundamentally_a (libgobject-2.0.so.0)
   #1 g_object_ref (libgobject-2.0.so.0)
   #2 fl_view_new_for_engine (libflutter_linux_gtk.so)
   #3 <Dart FFI frames>
   ```

   The same app outside the test binding opens the window fine.

### Expected

A live test binding (integration_test) should either:
- forward `engineId` to the real dispatcher and let tests opt into the platform windowing owner, or
- keep test windows and test text input consistent, so text input from a test-only view never reaches a platform plugin that cannot know that view.

### Context

Found in https://github.com/yvanvds/phi (subpatch editor windows, PR yvanvds/phi#555). Phi now routes text input to a stand-in in that test. It cannot test a real second native window end to end.

title: [Windowing][Windows] Closing a modal dialog while a satellite is open leaves the parent window permanently disabled
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Reproduced with the official reference app, `examples/multiple_windows`, on the `main` channel with `flutter config --enable-windowing`:

1. Run the example on Windows (`flutter run -d windows`).
2. Click **Satellite**. A satellite window opens, owned by the main window.
3. Click **Modal Dialog**. A modal dialog opens; the main window is disabled, as expected.
4. Close the modal dialog.
5. Close the satellite window.
6. Click the main window.

### Expected results

After step 4 the main window is enabled again and the satellite keeps behaving as a normal satellite. After step 5 the main window is still enabled.

### Actual results

- After step 4 the **main window stays disabled**, and the satellite becomes the only enabled window, as if the satellite were now the modal dialog.
- After step 5 the **main window stays disabled forever**: it ignores every click, with no dialog left open. The only way out is to kill the process.

macOS is not affected: the same steps behave correctly there, since the modal dialog is presented as a sheet and AppKit handles the modality.

### Analysis

From reading `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/windows/`:

1. `HostWindowDialog::HandleMessage` handles `WM_DESTROY` by calling `UpdateModalState()`, which walks up to the root window and calls `UpdateModalStateLayer()` on it.
2. `HostWindow::UpdateModalStateLayer()` treats **every** owned window returned by `GetOwnedWindows()` as part of the modal path. If the window has any owned window, it is disabled and only the most recently created child stays enabled. A satellite, as well as a popup or tooltip, is also an owned window, so after the modal is destroyed the root has one remaining owned window, the satellite. The root is therefore disabled and the satellite is treated as the active modal leaf.
3. Only `HostWindowDialog` recomputes the modal state on destruction. When the satellite is destroyed nothing calls `UpdateModalState()`, so the root keeps the `EnableWindow(root, false)` from step 2 permanently.

Possible fixes:

- When recomputing the modal state, only treat **modal dialogs** (dialogs with an owner) as part of the modal path. Non-dialog owned windows (satellite, popup, tooltip) should not cause their owner to be disabled.
- And/or recompute the modal state whenever any owned window is destroyed, not only dialogs.

### Code sample

The unmodified `examples/multiple_windows` app from the framework repository.

[vector_graphics_compiler] Support SVG vertex markers (<marker>)
body:
### Proposal

Currently, `vector_graphics_compiler` does not support SVG markers (`<marker>` element, and `marker`, `marker-start`, `marker-mid`, `marker-end` attributes). Path vertex markers are commonly used in SVGs for arrows, line terminals, diagrams, and vector charts.

We would like to add marker resolution and rendering support to `vector_graphics_compiler`.

title: [in_app_purchase_storekit] Expose revocationDate and revocationReason on SK2Transaction
body:
### Use case

When a StoreKit 2 transaction is refunded or revoked by Apple, `Transaction.revocationDate` and `Transaction.revocationReason` are set. `SK2Transaction` in `in_app_purchase_storekit` doesn't expose these fields, so apps can't detect revoked purchases from Dart and must fall back to server-side checks or native code.

### Proposal

Add `revocationDate` and `revocationReason` (`developerIssue` / `other`) to `SK2Transaction`, mapped from the native StoreKit 2 `Transaction`.

[web] `initializeEngine()` never settles when `canvaskit.wasm` (or `skwasm.wasm`) fails to download or compile
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms web --empty wasm_hang && cd wasm_hang`
2. Add `web/flutter_bootstrap.js` with the contents under **Code sample** (the template has no such file, so the build otherwise generates a default one). It starts the app through `onEntrypointLoaded`, shows an error message if `initializeEngine()` rejects, and logs the state of `initializeEngine()` after 30 s and 60 s.
3. Build with local CanvasKit: `flutter build web --release --no-web-resources-cdn`
4. Remove the CanvasKit module to simulate a failed download: `find build/web/canvaskit -name canvaskit.wasm -delete`
5. Serve the build: `python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/web`
6. Open http://localhost:8000/, open the console, and wait 60 s.

You can get the same result without deleting anything: serve `canvaskit.wasm` with a non-wasm MIME type (e.g. `text/plain`), serve a corrupt `canvaskit.wasm`, or, in a default (CDN) build, block the `www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/.../canvaskit.wasm` request.

### Expected results

`initializeEngine()` rejects with the fetch or compile error, so the page's `onEntrypointLoaded` error handling runs. Here, that handling replaces the page with "This app could not start: …".

That's what already happens when other parts of CanvasKit loading fail. I measured two such cases in all three browsers below, and in both `initializeEngine()` rejects and the page shows the message:

- `canvaskit.js` is missing (404): it rejects with `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: …/canvaskit.js` (Chromium; Firefox and WebKit give their own wording).
- `WebAssembly.compileStreaming` is missing (as in older Safari, see #158082; simulated by deleting it before load): it rejects with `TypeError: WebAssembly.compileStreaming is not a function`.

Only a failure of the `.wasm` download or compile is lost.

### Actual results

`initializeEngine()` never resolves or rejects. The browser logs an unhandled promise rejection, and the page stays blank (white). The app's error handling never runs, and `_flutter.loader.load()` gave no signal either: with this dart2js build it resolved immediately, before the failure.

This is not slowness. In instrumented runs of the 404 and corrupt-module cases, in all three browsers, nothing was left that could settle it: no request was in flight after the first second, the page had no pending timers or animation frames apart from the probe's own, `WebAssembly.instantiate` was never called, and `window.flutterCanvasKitLoaded` itself was still pending at 60 s (and at 180 s in a longer Chromium run).

Real-world triggers match the scenarios below: a server that doesn't send `application/wasm` for `.wasm`, a blocked or unreachable `www.gstatic.com`, a dropped connection, or a corrupted download. Each ends in a blank page that the app's own error handling can't see.

Measured with Flutter 3.47.7 stable, release build, headless browsers driven by Playwright 1.64. Each cell shows the state of `initializeEngine()` at 30 s and at 60 s, then the unhandled rejection reason.

| Scenario                                          | Chromium 156                                                                              | Firefox 157                                                                                   | WebKit 27.2 (Playwright build)                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Normal build                                      | resolved / resolved; app renders                                                          | resolved / resolved; app renders                                                              | resolved / resolved; app starts (scene canvas created) |
| `canvaskit.wasm` 404 (steps above)                | pending / pending; `TypeError: Failed to execute 'compile' on 'WebAssembly': HTTP status code is not ok`; blank | pending / pending; `TypeError: WebAssembly: Response has unsupported MIME type 'text/html;charset=utf-8' expected 'application/wasm'`; blank | pending / pending; `TypeError: Unexpected response MIME type. Expected 'application/wasm'`; blank |
| `canvaskit.wasm` is not valid wasm (`application/wasm`) | pending / pending; `CompileError: WebAssembly.compileStreaming(): expected magic word 00 61 73 6d, …`; blank | pending / pending; `CompileError: wasm validation error: at offset 4: failed to match magic number`; blank | pending / pending; `CompileError: WebAssembly.Module doesn't parse at byte 0: module doesn't start with '\0asm'`; blank |
| `canvaskit.wasm` served as `text/plain`           | pending / pending; `TypeError: … Incorrect response MIME type. Expected 'application/wasm'.`; blank | pending / pending; `TypeError: … unsupported MIME type 'text/plain' …`; blank             | pending / pending; `TypeError: Unexpected response MIME type. …`; blank               |
| CDN build, gstatic `canvaskit.wasm` request fails (network error) | pending / pending; `TypeError: Failed to fetch`; blank                    | pending / pending; `TypeError: NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.`; blank        | pending / pending; `TypeError: Load failed`; blank                                    |
| `WebAssembly.compileStreaming` deleted (contrast) | rejected / rejected; error message shown                                                  | rejected / rejected; error message shown                                                      | rejected / rejected; error message shown                                              |

The skwasm renderer has the same problem. I built with `flutter build web --release --wasm --no-web-resources-cdn` and deleted `skwasm.wasm`. In Chromium, `skwasm.wasm` returns 404 and an unhandled `TypeError: … HTTP status code is not ok` is logged. After that, `onEntrypointLoaded` is never called, `_flutter.loader.load()` stays pending after 60 s, and the page stays blank. In this setup Firefox and WebKit picked the dart2js/CanvasKit build, so they didn't exercise skwasm.

**Cause.** `createWasmInstantiator` in `flutter_js/src/instantiate_wasm.js` passes Emscripten an `instantiateWasm` callback that does its async work in a fire-and-forget IIFE with no `catch`. If the fetch or compile fails, `successCallback` is never called and the rejection goes nowhere. These lines are unchanged on `master` as of 8980aca77d (2026-11-04), and the pattern goes back to the file's creation in [flutter/engine#49037](https://github.com/flutter-team-archive/engine/pull/49037):

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/8980aca77decee63beb550c13fe6ac0b6085b205/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/instantiate_wasm.js#L106-L114

```js
  const modulePromise = WebAssembly.compileStreaming(getResponse());
  return (imports, successCallback) => {
    (async () => {
      const module = await modulePromise;
      const instance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(module, imports);
      successCallback(instance, module);
    })();
    return {};
  };
```

Emscripten's generated glue (`canvaskit.js`, `skwasm.js`) rejects its module promise only if `instantiateWasm` throws synchronously; its own default instantiation path, which this hook replaces, ends in `.catch(readyPromiseReject)`. When the failure is asynchronous, the factory promise awaited in [`canvaskit_loader.js`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/8980aca77decee63beb550c13fe6ac0b6085b205/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/canvaskit_loader.js#L36-L40) and [`skwasm_loader.js`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/8980aca77decee63beb550c13fe6ac0b6085b205/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/skwasm_loader.js#L35-L41) never settles. As a result, `window.flutterCanvasKitLoaded` (and through it `initializeEngine()`) and `deps.skwasm` stay pending. The two contrast cases do reject because their errors arise inside `loadCanvasKit`'s async function itself: the missing-`compileStreaming` `TypeError` is thrown synchronously by `createWasmInstantiator`, and a missing `canvaskit.js` rejects the awaited `import()`.

**Suggested fix (untested).** Pass a failure of `modulePromise` or `WebAssembly.instantiate` back to the loader. For example, `createWasmInstantiator` could also expose the failure as a promise, and `loadCanvasKit`/`loadSkwasm` could race the Emscripten factory against it. Then `flutterCanvasKitLoaded` rejects and with it `initializeEngine()`, and for skwasm `deps.skwasm` rejects and with it `load()`.

This is a concrete, still-open case of #102265 ("Reject flutter.js promises when critical assets fail to download", open since 2022, before the current loader). With today's loader, a failed `canvaskit.js` download does reject (measured above), but a failed or invalid `.wasm` still doesn't.

Related, but not the same: #158082 (older Safari without `compileStreaming`, where startup does reject) and #193505 (CanvasKit assets returning 404 under `flutter test --platform chrome`). #157585, closed for lack of a reproduction, looks like this bug seen in production: `Uncaught (in promise) CompileError: WebAssembly.compileStreaming()` from a self-hosted `canvaskit.wasm`, and an app that never loads.

Today, an app can only detect this case with its own timer or a global `unhandledrejection` listener.

### Code sample

`lib/main.dart` is unmodified `flutter create --empty` output. `web/flutter_bootstrap.js`:

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```js
{{flutter_js}}
{{flutter_build_config}}

// Records whether initializeEngine() settles, and every uncaught error.
const probe = (window.probe = { engine: "not called", events: [] });
const log = (message) => {
  probe.events.push(message);
  console.log("[probe] " + message);
};
window.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", (e) => log("unhandledrejection: " + e.reason));
window.addEventListener("error", (e) => log("error: " + e.message));
for (const seconds of [30, 60]) {
  setTimeout(() => log(`after ${seconds} s: initializeEngine ${probe.engine}`), seconds * 1000);
}

_flutter.loader.load({
  onEntrypointLoaded: async (engineInitializer) => {
    probe.engine = "pending";
    try {
      const appRunner = await engineInitializer.initializeEngine();
      probe.engine = "resolved";
      log("initializeEngine resolved");
      await appRunner.runApp();
    } catch (e) {
      probe.engine = "rejected: " + e;
      log("initializeEngine rejected: " + e);
      document.body.textContent = "This app could not start: " + e;
    }
  },
}).then(() => log("load() resolved"), (e) => log("load() rejected: " + e));
```

</details>

title: [iOS] availableCameras() intermittently fails to return back cameras
body:
### Steps to reproduce

There is an intermittent issue on iOS where `availableCameras()` fails
to return cameras with `CameraLensDirection.back`.

This issue occurs only on iOS and has been observed on multiple devices,
including:

-   iPhone SE (3rd generation) - `iPhone14,6`
-   iPhone 12 - `iPhone13,2`
-   iPhone 15 - `iPhone15,4`

The issue occurs intermittently and cannot be reproduced consistently.

Interestingly, even when this issue occurs, other camera applications
can access the back camera without any problems. This suggests that the
back camera itself is functioning normally.

### Steps to Reproduce

1.  Launch the application on an iOS device.
2.  Call `availableCameras()` during `initState()`.
3.  Check the returned list of cameras.

title: [camera_android_camerax] Fatal "Unsupported value: ProcessCameraProvider" when getInstance completes after onDetachedFromEngine
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

camera (Android implementation: camera_android_camerax)

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

No. The analysis below is against camera_android_camerax 0.7.4+6. I checked the CHANGELOG up to 0.7.6+1 and saw no entry for this path.

### Dependency versions

```yaml
camera: 0.12.0+2
camera_android_camerax: 0.7.4+6
```

### Steps to reproduce

This is a production crash (1 event so far). I have not reproduced it deterministically. The mechanism below comes from reading the released plugin sources.

1. Call `availableCameras()` (this reaches `ProcessCameraProvider.getInstance`) shortly after app start. The app is idle on its home screen, with no `CameraController` and no camera open.
2. While the `ListenableFuture` from `ProcessCameraProvider.getInstance(context)` is still pending, the Activity is destroyed and the engine detaches. `CameraAndroidCameraxPlugin.onDetachedFromEngine` runs `setIgnoreCallsToDart(true)` and `tearDown()`.
3. The future completes on the main executor (`ProcessCameraProviderProxyApi.java:48`), so `ResultCompat.success(provider, callback)` encodes the reply.

### Expected results

The late reply is dropped (or logged), because calls to Dart are being ignored after detach.

### Actual results

The app crashes with a fatal `IllegalArgumentException` on the main thread:

1. In `CameraXLibraryPigeonProxyApiBaseCodec.writeValue`, the `ProcessCameraProvider` branch (`CameraXLibrary.g.kt:953`) calls `pigeon_newInstance`.
2. Because `ignoreCallsToDart` is true, `pigeon_newInstance` returns `ignore-calls-error` without adding the instance (`CameraXLibrary.g.kt:2654`). That failure is only logged.
3. Execution then reaches the final `when`: `containsInstance(value)` is false, so it throws `Unsupported value` (`CameraXLibrary.g.kt:1219`).

title: Windows: tool passes unescaped cmd.exe metacharacters to .bat/.cmd invocations (BatBadBut class)
body:
## What

On Windows, the Flutter tool invokes batch wrappers (`gradlew.bat`,
`apkanalyzer.bat`, `sdkmanager.bat`, `avdmanager.bat`, `flutter.bat`) with
arguments derived from project paths, `--target`, `--build-number`, filesystem
roots, etc. Launching a `.bat`/`.cmd` implicitly routes it through `cmd.exe`,
but `dart:io` escapes process arguments only for the C runtime's
`CommandLineToArgvW` rules, never for `cmd.exe`. Shell metacharacters
(`& | < > ^ " % ! ( )`, newlines) in an argument are therefore reparsed by
`cmd.exe` as command syntax rather than literal data — the "BatBadBut" class
(CVE-2024-24576 and related, patched in Rust/Node.js/PHP in 2024).

## Why it matters

Building or running an untrusted project on Windows (crafted path/name/`--target`)
can lead to arbitrary command execution during an ordinary `flutter build`/run.
Windows only; not exploitable on macOS/Linux.

## Scope of the proposed fix

Defence-in-depth hardening in the tool: a central fail-closed guard in
`ErrorHandlingProcessManager` that rejects `cmd.exe` metacharacters in arguments
to `.bat`/`.cmd` targets and to `runInShell: true` invocations on Windows. The
underlying `dart:io` escaping gap is the root cause and is being raised with the
Dart SDK team separately.

## Disclosure

First reported via Google OSS VRP (IssueTracker 581878275); acknowledged as a
genuine product vulnerability, closed only under the Oct 1 2026 rule change
limiting OSS VRP to supply-chain reports, with guidance to report directly to
the Flutter team. PR to follow.

[framework][platform-windows] TapGestureRecognizer gets stuck after native dialog swallows pointer up events
body:
## Problem

On Windows, when a native modal dialog (file picker, folder picker, etc.) is opened from a Flutter app, the host platform swallows `PointerUpEvent` and `PointerCancelEvent` for any active gesture. This leaves `TapGestureRecognizer` stuck tracking a stale `primaryPointer` with `state == possible`.

After the dialog is closed, **all subsequent taps with new pointer ids are silently ignored** because `addAllowedPointer` only accepts new pointers when `state == ready`:

```dart
void addAllowedPointer(PointerDownEvent event) {
  if (state == GestureRecognizerState.ready) {  // blocked by stale pointer
```

## Reproduction

```dart
ElevatedButton(
  onPressed: () async {
    FilePickerResult? result = await FilePicker.platform.pickFiles();
    // After canceling the picker (ESC or X), subsequent taps are dead.
  },
  child: Text('Open'),
)
```

Steps:
1. Run a Flutter Windows desktop app with a button that opens a native file picker
2. Click the button — file picker opens
3. **Close the file picker without selecting anything** (ESC or X button)
4. Try tapping any button or interactive widget in the app

**Expected**: Taps work normally after the dialog closes.  
**Actual**: Nothing responds to taps. All `PointerDownEvent`s with new pointer ids are silently ignored by `TapGestureRecognizer`. The user must restart the app.

Note: Selecting a file and confirming does not trigger the issue — only canceling does.

## Root Cause

`BaseTapGestureRecognizer.addAllowedPointer` guards new pointer downs with `if (state == GestureRecognizerState.ready)`. When a stale pointer sequence is left unresolved by a native dialog swallowing up/cancel events, the state machine never returns to `ready`. Every new pointer down is ignored forever.

## Proposed Fix

Force-resolve the stale pointer sequence before the guarded path when:
1. `state != GestureRecognizerState.ready` (we're stuck)
2. `_down != null` (we're tracking something)
3. The new pointer id differs from `_down!.pointer` (this is genuinely a new gesture, not a repeat)
4. The stale pointer has persisted longer than `kLongPressTimeout` (500ms) — meaning it can no longer form a valid tap (taps are down→up within 500ms; anything beyond is either a long press handled by a different recognizer or stale)

Using `kLongPressTimeout` instead of an arbitrary threshold preserves the correct FIFO semantics for legitimate overlapping multi-touch gestures (which arrive within milliseconds), while correctly recovering from dialog-swallowed stale pointers.

## Fix Code

In `packages/flutter/lib/src/gestures/tap.dart`, `BaseTapGestureRecognizer.addAllowedPointer`:

```dart
@override
void addAllowedPointer(PointerDownEvent event) {
  if (state != GestureRecognizerState.ready &&
      _down != null &&
      _down!.pointer != event.pointer &&
      event.timeStamp - _down!.timeStamp > kLongPressTimeout) {
    final int stalePointer = _down!.pointer;
    resolve(GestureDisposition.rejected);
    stopTrackingPointer(stalePointer);
    _reset();
  }

  if (state == GestureRecognizerState.ready) {
    // ... existing code unchanged
```

## Test

A new test `stale_pointer_recovery_test.dart` simulates this exact scenario. It:
1. Dispatches pointer 1 down with timeStamp 0, never dispatches up
2. Advances FakeAsync clock by 2 seconds (> 500ms threshold)
3. Dispatches pointer 2 down + up
4. Expects `onTap` to fire for pointer 2

This test **fails on master** (pointer 2 is ignored) and **passes with the fix**.

All 33 existing `tap_test.dart` tests continue to pass — including the FIFO/FILO overlapping tap tests, confirming the `kLongPressTimeout` threshold correctly distinguishes stale pointers from legitimate multi-touch overlaps.

title: [Proposal] Decouple NetworkImage and NetworkAssetBundle from dart:io
body:
We should consider allowing users to bring their own HTTP networking to Flutter, so that if a vulnerability was found, they could quickly migrate to a secure HTTP package without needing to upgrade Dart and Flutter.

There appear to be only two places where Flutter uses dart:io to access the network: [NetworkImage](https://main-api.flutter.dev/flutter/painting/NetworkImage-class.html) and [NetworkAssetBundle](https://main-api.flutter.dev/flutter/services/NetworkAssetBundle-class.html). I propose that we add a parameter to allow users to pass their own HttpClient, or their own `load` method.

title: [go_router] App hangs when leaving a nested ShellRoute whose builder reads GoRouterState.of (regression in 18.1.1)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `MaterialApp.router` from `package:material_ui`. With `package:flutter/material.dart`'s `MaterialApp` the same routes do not hang.
2. Use an outer `ShellRoute` whose builder returns a widget with a new key on every build (`UniqueKey()`).
3. Nest a second `ShellRoute` under one of its `GoRoute`s. Its builder widget calls `GoRouterState.of(context)` in `build`.
4. `go` to a route inside the nested shell, then `go` back to the parent route.

The code sample below is a widget test; `flutter test` never finishes on step 4.

### Expected results

Navigation back to `/home` completes, as it does on go_router 18.1.0.

### Actual results

The UI thread hangs: no frames, no input, no error or log output. Happens on 18.1.1, 18.1.2 and 18.1.3; 18.1.0 is fine.

Pausing the hung app (Flutter web, debug) always lands in `GoRouterState.of`, called from the nested shell widget's `build`. At that point the `while (true)` loop's `context` is a `Navigator` element, and its `ModalRoute`'s page is not in the `GoRouterStateRegistry`. `Navigator.maybeOf` on a Navigator's own element returns that same Navigator, so `context = state.context` never changes and the loop never ends.

#159593 reports a hang in the same `GoRouterState.of` loop, reached by passing a `Navigator`'s own context from a `NavigatorObserver`; its sample also hangs on 18.1.0. Here the loop is reached from a plain `GoRouterState.of(context)` in a shell builder widget, which worked until 18.1.1. Making the loop throw instead of spinning would fix the hang in both, but this case would still fail: since 18.1.1 the shell's page is no longer found while leaving the nested shell.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

class Shell extends StatelessWidget {
  const Shell({super.key, required this.child});

  final Widget child;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Column(
      children: [
        Text('shell: ${GoRouterState.of(context).uri}'),
        Expanded(child: child),
      ],
    );
  }
}

void main() {
  testWidgets('leaving a nested ShellRoute whose builder reads GoRouterState.of', (tester) async {
    final router = GoRouter(
      initialLocation: '/home',
      routes: [
        ShellRoute(
          // A new key on every rebuild of the outer shell.
          builder: (context, state, child) => Scaffold(key: UniqueKey(), body: child),
          routes: [
            GoRoute(
              path: '/home',
              builder: (context, state) => const Text('home'),
              routes: [
                ShellRoute(
                  builder: (context, state, child) => Shell(child: child),
                  routes: [GoRoute(path: 'inner', builder: (context, state) => const Text('inner'))],
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ],
    );
    addTearDown(router.dispose);
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp.router(routerConfig: router));

    router.go('/home/inner');
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(find.text('inner'), findsOneWidget);

    router.go('/home'); // 18.1.1+: never returns
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(find.text('home'), findsOneWidget);
  });
}
```

</details>

</details>

title: [Google3 Bug]: [Flutter Android Engine] Heuristic fallback to populate ViewNode.hint in AssistStructure from enclosed/overlapping placeholder Text for older Flutter versions
body:
### Help us understand the severity of this issue

- [ ] causing severe production issues e.g. malfunctions or data loss
- [ ] blocking next binary release
- [ ] blocking a client feature launch within a quarter
- [x] nice-to-have but does not block a launch within the next quarter

### Steps to reproduce

Background & Context:

We previously identified an issue where Flutter drops visual placeholder/hint text from Android's virtual AssistStructure (ViewNode.getHint() == null) when apps build custom input components using EditableText:
- Public GitHub Issue (Accepted by Framework team): https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/194470
- Real-world impact on Autofill: b/539911597 (Slickdeals app login field detection failure)

The Dart framework team has agreed to add support for specifying autofill configurations on EditableText directly (EditableText.autofillConfiguration / EditableText.autofillTextInputConfiguration).

The Problem for Existing / Older Flutter Apps:
While the framework-side fix addresses new apps or apps that upgrade to newer Flutter versions, thousands of Flutter apps currently in production (e.g. Slickdeals, net.slickdeals.android) were compiled with older Flutter versions.

In these apps:
1. Developers built custom text fields using Stack [ Text(placeholder), EditableText(...) ].

2. In Flutter's Accessibility hierarchy, AccessibilityBridge correctly renders the visual placeholder as an enclosed virtual TextView inside or overlapping the virtual EditText node:
   - HSV Snapshot: https://hsv.googleplex.com/4838541719764992?node=54
   - Screenshot showing child TextView in HSV: https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/66cht8qbbdik0

3. However, in TextInputPlugin.onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure(), only the flat EditText is emitted, and child.setHint(...) is skipped because autofill.hintText is null from Dart:
   ```java
   // io/flutter/plugin/editing/TextInputPlugin.java:
   if (autofill.hintText != null) {
     child.setHint(autofill.hintText);
   }
   ```

As a result, ViewNode.getHint() remains null in Android's AssistStructure, breaking autofill heuristic detection (such as Google Autofill's HintProcessor).

Feature Request for Flutter Android Engine:

Can the Android Engine (TextInputPlugin.java) implement a heuristic fallback when populating ViewStructure in onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure()?

Proposed Logic: If autofill.hintText is null:

Query the corresponding node in AccessibilityBridge / Semantics tree.
If there is a child or overlapping text node (e.g. a placeholder Text widget within the same bounding box/enclosing Stack):
- Extract that text string.
- Populate child.setHint(fallbackHintText).

Benefits:

Backward Compatibility: Automatically fixes Android AssistStructure hint text for thousands of already-deployed Flutter apps in the ecosystem.
Instant Autofill Quality Improvement: Allows Android Autofill providers (Google Autofill, 1Password, Bitwarden, etc.) to accurately detect and classify fields without requiring third-party developers to upgrade Flutter or rewrite custom input components.

### Expected results

1. Engine-Level Heuristic Fallback:
   - In `TextInputPlugin.java` (`onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure`), when `autofill.hintText == null`, the Android engine queries the corresponding `SemanticsNode` / `AccessibilityBridge` tree for the input field.
   - If an overlapping or child text element (e.g., a placeholder `Text` widget sharing the bounding box or enclosed within the same `Stack`) is detected:
     - Extracts the text content from that semantic node.
     - Calls `child.setHint(fallbackHintText)` on the virtual `ViewStructure.ViewNode`.
2. Populated `ViewNode.hint` in Android `AssistStructure`:
   - The emitted virtual node in the Android OS `AssistStructure` contains the visual placeholder text in `ViewNode.getHint()` (e.g., `"Email or Username"`, `"Password"`).
3. Automatic Ecosystem Backward-Compatibility:
   - Android Autofill services can reliably classify input fields and surface autofill suggestions across thousands of production Flutter apps without requiring third-party app developers to upgrade Flutter SDK versions or refactor custom UI widgets.

### Actual results

1. `ViewNode.getHint()` is `null` in `AssistStructure`:
   - When a Flutter app builds a custom input field (e.g., using `Stack [ Text(placeholder), EditableText(...) ]`) or is built with an older Flutter version where `autofill.hintText` is null from Dart, `TextInputPlugin.java` (`onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure`) skips setting the hint:
     ```java
     if (autofill.hintText != null) {
       child.setHint(autofill.hintText);
     }
     ```
   - As a result, the virtual `ViewStructure` emitted to the Android framework has `ViewNode.getHint() == null`.
2. Visual Placeholder Dropped Despite Being Present in Accessibility/Semantics:
   - Even though the placeholder text is visually rendered on screen and correctly represented in Flutter's `AccessibilityBridge` / Semantics tree (e.g., as an enclosed/overlapping virtual `TextView`, as seen in HSV: https://hsv.googleplex.com/4838541719764992?node=54), it is completely omitted from the Autofill virtual node.
3. Downstream Autofill Failure:
   - Android Autofill services (Google Autofill, Bitwarden, 1Password, etc.) cannot inspect the field's visual label or placeholder.
   - Heuristic classification engines (such as Google Autofill's `HintProcessor`) fail to detect the field type, resulting in missing autofill suggestions on login/registration forms (e.g., Slickdeals b/539911597).

Relaunch and repeat if it renders correctly. ### Expected results The yellow first page is replaced by the green second page. ### Actual results The Flutter button updates and `onPageFinished` fires, but the WebView keeps showing the yellow first page. The default Android WebView mode, Texture Layer Hybrid Composition, renders the native WebView into a texture that Flutter displays. Switching to hybrid composition with `--dart-define=HYBRID_COMPOSITION=true` makes the green page appear. The failure is triggered by the Huawei fallback in `FlutterRenderer.createSurfaceProducer()`. Its `!hasAndroidHardwareBufferDefect()` condition selects `SurfaceTextureSurfaceProducer` on Huawei API 29. Bypassing that condition to select `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer` achieves the expected result. [Producer selection](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/737ba8f885dc774b53b442759999a312c9461e4e/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/renderer/FlutterRenderer.java#L225-L249) · [Huawei check](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/737ba8f885dc774b53b442759999a312c9461e4e/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/renderer/FlutterRenderer.java#L70-L89) Using Hybrid composition for the webview also works as a workaround. The condition causing the problem came from the video playback fix for #166481. ### Code sample

"Show first page" : "Show second page"), ), Expanded( child: WebViewWidget.fromPlatformCreationParams( params: AndroidWebViewWidgetCreationParams( controller: _controller.platform, displayWithHybridComposition: hybridComposition, ), ), ), ], ), ); } } ``` ```
